this is a very important report on the future of europe. we must continue to build on the development of industry, which is the main source of gdp. for years, europe dominated the rest of the global competition. it is absolutely essential to invest in small and medium-sized enterprises, to renew innovation strategies, to create genuine research and development centres that will be able to continue to be a source of innovation and new ideas in europe. that is why it is so important to prepare a strategy modelled on the strategy of other countries in the world that are competing with europe. i therefore believe that the european union should jointly prepare and implement this strategy, first of all by removing all barriers. the main thing is to increase access to capital, reduce red tape and, above all, invest huge money in industrial innovation and research.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on reindustrialising europe to promote competitiveness and sustainable growth. the economic crisis has caused severe losses in the industrial sector, with as many as 3.8 million people losing their jobs. despite the situation, industry remains one of the main drivers of growth in the european union. however, to boost growth again, europe needs a strong and long-term industrial strategy today. given the increasing industrial development in emerging economies, the european union must focus its efforts on investing in innovation and developing a green strategy. the reindustrialisation plan must aim to reduce energy and resource costs, making european industry more competitive. however, this cannot be achieved without increasing the pool of funding for research development and innovation investments. i believe that the allocation of the appropriate funds to these objectives will increase the competitiveness of european enterprises on world markets and contribute to the creation of new highly skilled jobs in europe.
in writing. - i welcomed the fact that the european parliament had adopted a resolution on reindustrialising europe to support its competitiveness and sustainable development. there is an urgent need to rebuild and modernise the eu's industrial base, which would increase its competitiveness at regional and global level. the resolution draws attention to the fact that the availability of energy is a fundamental element of the strategy of industrialization. as i mentioned in the debate, it is the continuing rise in energy prices that is one of the main barriers to the reindustrialisation of europe, reducing the competitiveness of european companies on the global market. in addition, the burden of energy costs and the resulting complexity and instability of european regulation are contributing to the relocation of industrial enterprises outside the european union.
in writing. - europe is losing industry to other parts of the world where production is more profitable. the idea that we have a 'post-industrial' development based solely on services is not true, because there is no development without material production. is the union economy sufficiently competitive to allow for a real industrial recovery? what is the structure and the areas of activity? when analysing global competitiveness, we see that the cost components are higher in europe than for global competitors. this situation could only be remedied by product innovation, which depends on energy, material and organisational efficient technologies and efficient business processes. but we're not innovative enough. the emerging powers are making progress in areas like itc, nanotechnology, biotechnology. what market niches will the eu reindustrialisation be based on? the industry has been dominated by monopolistic multinational companies, which do not favour the creation of smes, with which they compete fiercely. europe needs solutions that will revive local industry, industry that will be able to meet demand competitively, based on local raw materials and a traditional work culture. this applies to agricultural, forestry and mineral raw materials, e.g. for construction; it applies to local energy. in the hope that the project under discussion will initiate action to re-industrialize, i voted yes.
in writing. − the global crisis has hit european economies hard, also negatively affecting the industrial sector, which plays a key role in building prosperity and creating jobs in eu member states. a comprehensive strategy for growth and sustainable investment leading to economic recovery is therefore needed. european industrial policy must focus on challenges such as: lack of investment in research and development, rising energy prices, red tape and difficulties in accessing finance, lack of adequately qualified workers. the rise industrial recovery strategy for a sustainable europe should support technological, business, financial, environmental and social innovation, while leading to the emergence of new innovative products and services, new business models and creative entrepreneurs and enterprises, the creation of new jobs and decent work, and contributing to industrial renewal, economic dynamism, consumer confidence and competitiveness. i also welcome the attention paid to the problems of small and medium-sized enterprises, which have been most affected by the crisis, and to the need to provide them with comprehensive support in the reindustrialisation process, including through the reform of trade defence instruments.
in writing. - i voted for mr bütikofer's report because i believe that european industry has great potential. i am therefore glad that this subject is now in the parliament's interest. although the economic crisis led to a reduction in industrial employment in the european union, it was also noted that the more industrialised european economies fared better during the crisis. however, we must remember that we are in a post-industrial era and the process of reindustrialisation must be adapted to the current economic realities both in europe and in the world. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that we need a holistic approach that focuses on creating an innovative and competitive industry. it should be noted that production is now decentralised, distributed and divided into small activities and stages. local production needs different support than large industrial plants. support for smes is key here. the main priority for such establishments is access to finance and the removal of bureaucratic barriers in order to unlock their full potential and contribute to the creation of new jobs, including for young people. cohesion policy can also play an important role here, as it can support smart specialisation, innovation and regional business incubators in the new financial perspective. a complementary element of horizon 2020 may be provided in this respect.
in writing. - the question of industry and reindustrialisation is a specific one in that it is not just an internal community matter, which the community itself has the greatest influence on. as players like china formulate their next multi-year industrial development plans, we should not just sit back and wait for the effects of these changes to reach us. despite the evolution of european economies, industry still accounts for the majority of exports and private sector investment in research and development. we should now focus not only on providing a favourable framework for the development of industry from the regional to the eu level, but also on working with the sector to move towards a low-carbon economy. factors such as development, environmental protection and necessary investments should be weighed. in view of the particular attention paid in the countries of the union to the environment and to the protection of the health and life of citizens, attention to industrial development must go hand in hand with investment in innovative solutions and the upgrading of the level of qualification of specialists. increased labour productivity and measures to improve resource efficiency are good signals, as they are important factors in improving the competitiveness of european industry. a stable and growing industry also provides jobs, which not only helps it to grow, but also creates a demand for skilled workers, thus alleviating social problems.
in writing. - modern europe needs innovative proposals and best practice to become an industrial powerhouse with a large market for new jobs. all actions must be deliberate and evolutionary in nature. the main issues to be discussed are competition and overproduction in industry. europe is witnessing the rise of new industrial powers that will soon overtake it. many member states are embroiled in economic disputes, which very often prevent quick and joint decisions from being taken when they are most needed. a prime example is the lack of consensus on energy issues. individual countries cannot be both competitors and partners for each other. we must break down these barriers and work towards a european industrial agreement. it's also worth encouraging innovation and completely changing the way we think about industrial secrecy.
in writing. - europe needs a strong and competitive industry today to help us get out of the crisis. without the right conditions for business, we can forget about any development. so to talk about the reindustrialisation of europe, we should first of all talk about the mistakes we have made in recent times. the energy and climate package is particularly dangerous. they will cause energy prices to rise and industry to continue to flee abroad. another mistake is to over-regulate the economy. the additional environmental standards, plus the administrative burden, mean that entrepreneurs spend their time filling out paperwork instead of thinking about development. the rapporteur has mentioned all this in his report, while stressing the importance of the green revolution for improving the situation. i don't agree with that kind of thinking, and that's why i voted against it.
in writing. − the governing council of the european central bank (ecb) adopted an opinion on the recommendation of the council of the european union concerning the appointment of a new member of the executive board of the ecb. the governing council did not object to the nomination of sabine lautenschläger, who is a person of recognised standing and professional experience in the field of finance and banking, as required by article 283 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the european council, acting by a majority of its euro area members, shall decide on the appointment after receiving the opinions of the governing council and the european parliament. the ecb's opinion, which will shortly be published in the official journal of the european union, is available on the ecb's website in all official eu languages.
in writing. − an application for waiver of the immunity of a member of the european parliament is generally submitted to the president of the european parliament by a court, a public prosecutor's office or the foreign affairs ministry. the final waiver of immunity shall be decided upon by the ep plenary. this procedure shall also apply if the member does not wish to avail himself of the protection. a member may not be formally charged without his immunity being waived.
mr. chairman, please! the words of the british prime minister on immigrants cannot go unheeded by the eu institutions, and above all by the european parliament. in a free europe, we cannot build bridges and create barriers that undermine the right to free movement of people. no one can be discriminated against on the grounds of nationality and this right should not be undermined by any european policy. my countrymen, by working in the uk, by paying taxes to the uk system, by buying goods and services, contribute to gdp growth and are entitled to social benefits. the proposed resolution is a very important signal to the citizens of the european union, as it says that the european parliament does not accept that any country in the european union practices a policy of discrimination. i am therefore very pleased that parliament has decided to adopt this resolution by a large majority, and i am also pleased that i was able to vote in favour of it.
mr. chairman, please! the principle of free movement of persons, including workers, is one of the greatest achievements of european integration, a kind of foundation on which the european community as a whole is based. however, in recent weeks, there has been a growing number of proposals from some countries to restrict migration policies and migration for economic reasons. such demands must be strongly opposed. i look to the european commission to take an active and unambiguous stance in defence of this remarkable achievement of europe's post-war generations. european integration should be for all the inhabitants of the continent and they should not be discriminated against on grounds of nationality, and unfortunately such declarations have also been made. the mobility of skilled workers has so far brought tangible benefits to the european economy as a whole. the migration is mainly of young people, active in their work, and i am not convinced by the argument that the national welfare systems are overburdened.
in writing. - we have been hearing for some time about the legal solutions proposed by the uk government which discriminate against poles living there in the use of social benefits. we also hear anti-immigrant rhetoric from politicians of all parties. while respecting the sovereignty of each country in social policy, i would like to remind you that eu member states have also undertaken commitments, including the obligation to treat all eu citizens equally. the changes proposed by the uk government are typical demonstration measures, harsh on eu citizens working there, but of little real significance to its budget. the burden of social transfers to poles is the benefit for only 25000 children. polish unemployed account for only 1% of the country's welfare recipients. at the same time, poles make a significant contribution to uk gdp. we cannot choose from the european union only those freedoms that suit us, in this case - yes - for the movement of capital, no - for the movement of people. in this case, the marginal benefit is at the expense of the fundamental principle. i have always encouraged my fellow citizens to be active citizens, both in their own country and in any place in europe where they have the right to do so. i would encourage them to use this power in the next european elections and to express their views on prime minister cameron's proposal.
in writing. − the free movement of persons within the european union is one of the fundamental rights of eu citizens and a guarantee of the smooth functioning of the single market. the free movement of workers is one of the most effective tools in the fight against the global economic crisis and the challenges of a changing world. the benefits of the free movement of mobile workers in the eu are visible across europe, and it is a cornerstone of eu integration and economic development. i therefore support the joint motion for a resolution and the call for the abolition of all forms of discrimination against mobile workers in the eu, and for the illegal exploitation of the link between the right to free movement of persons for professional purposes and alleged abuses of social security systems. i also support parliament's call for the strict enforcement of eu law in all member states to ensure equal treatment for all eu workers and non-discrimination in access to employment, in the workplace and in terms of working conditions, pay, leave and social and tax benefits, thereby ensuring fair competition between businesses. i also support the call to ensure that any unjustified restrictions or obstacles to the free movement of workers are eliminated.
in writing. − in the current complex situation, when european economies have a chance to return to growth, the effective functioning of the common market is of the utmost importance. the infringement of market mechanisms and one of the fundamental freedoms of europe for propaganda purposes is a dangerous manipulation that can have serious negative economic consequences. as history shows, crises and economic hardships foster nationalistic, xenophobic attitudes and the dictates of demagogy over rational governance. one of the european union's tasks is to ensure that these dangerous trends do not disrupt the political and economic order of the community. as statistics show, polish workers in the uk contribute to gdp growth and pay taxes in the uk to finance their entitlements. migration is an important factor for the proper functioning of the european labour market and its positive impact cannot be undermined by populist activities.
in writing. − freedom of movement is one of the fundamental freedoms on which the european union is founded. this freedom is also guaranteed by the treaty, which means that its non-observance is a breach of the treaty principles, as is any restriction on it, including the restriction of migration volumes. it should be borne in mind that despite the populist statements of many prominent european politicians, migration, mostly related to labour mobility, brings many benefits to the host countries, also from an economic point of view. in the run-up to the european elections, the rhetoric of limiting migration will certainly be welcomed by citizens tired of the crisis, unemployment, but it is dangerous because it can lead to the development of xenophobic or even racist attitudes. i supported this resolution because i do not agree with the restriction of the fundamental freedoms which the treaties guarantee to eu citizens.
in writing. - the free movement of people is the foundation of the european single market. it is a right that belongs to all citizens of each eu member state. i strongly disagree with the positions of some european leaders, led by prime minister david cameron, who are calling for this freedom to be curtailed. such statements are an expression of weakness and blatant injustice towards immigrants who, through their hard work, build not only their own prosperity but also the prosperity of the host country. i am pleased that in the resolution parliament calls on the member states to use the resources of the union funds on migration: the european social fund, whose share in national envelopes we have increased to over 23%, and the european regional development fund. these funds, together with the cohesion policy for the next 7 years, can help to promote integration, social inclusion and poverty reduction. we need to focus on tackling unemployment across the eu, because it, along with the poverty that goes with it, is the root cause of migration. instead of arguing about the fundamental freedoms of every eu citizen, we should focus on the fight for a decent life for all europeans. it should not be forgotten that the fight against social dumping, the respect for the rights of posted workers and the protection of the social benefits of migrant workers are also integral elements of the discussion on the free movement of persons. for these reasons, i support the motion for a resolution.
in writing. - i strongly supported the resolution on the right to free movement in the eu. in the context of the debate on this issue, three key issues deserve special attention. first, free movement within the union is a fundamental right guaranteed to union citizens by the treaties, from which both workers and the economies of the member states benefit. second, it is not true that immigrants are over-reaching on social rights. in most eu countries, citizens of other member states do not receive social benefits more than citizens of the host member state. this is confirmed by the commission's investigation. moreover, in the united kingdom, for example, the taxes paid by european union immigrants exceed by 37 percent the social security benefits they receive in return. there is a small percentage of social tourists who take advantage of the situation, which reflects negatively on the entire immigrant community and creates a false stereotype. third, europe will soon begin to feel the effects of an ageing population and a shrinking workforce. already today, despite the high level of unemployment across the union, there are some 2 million vacancies available. the negative, discriminatory policies towards immigrants in some eu member states are very short-sighted.
in writing. − the european union boasts a number of freedoms for its citizens, and the freedom to leave, combined with the right to reside and work in another eu country, is one of the fundamental freedoms. the establishment of an appropriate framework to ensure full mobility in the internal labour market has a significant impact on the state of national economies and contributes to the competitiveness of the union as a whole. despite the sometimes expressed concerns about the influx of workers from the so-called 'new eu', their presence has had a positive impact on the economic development of the countries they have gone to. moreover, mobile workers from these countries did not have a significant impact on wage levels or unemployment rates in the host countries. freedom of movement for workers does not mean simply taking up a better-paid job in another country, as this mechanism can help to neutralise the negative effects of the economic crisis in the longer term. it should also be noted that the influx of foreign workers is not the cause of labour market problems, structural problems or the crisis in the labour market. there is a widespread tendency to blame immigrants for various adverse events, but these attitudes are often based on emotional factors. , so it's hard to treat them as arguments, even if they're shared by larger social groups.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on respect for the fundamental right of free movement in the eu (2013/2960(rsp)). this motion outlines a fundamental freedom of all eu citizens and their right to live and work wherever they please in the union. without question, there remain some sensitive areas but it is vital that the basic freedom of movement remains intact. the primary concern is that certain member states will implement legislation complicating said movement for some groups which, in turn, will result in the breakdown of that freedom. coincidentally poles have been singled out as one group that is taking full advantage of this freedom and is somehow blamed for problems in their new environment. while i would hope that my fellow citizens would stay in poland and contribute to our continued growth, it is preposterous to limit their freedom to relocate and then accuse them of not contributing. this situation is but one of the problems facing free movement but i feel that it illustrates the issues facing member states as more and more citizens pursue employment opportunities or other goals.
in writing. − the single market covers the whole area of the eu without internal borders, where goods, people, services and capital can move freely. it was created by the abolition of internal border controls. the single market recalls that the union is primarily a sphere of activity for competing firms. from this point of view, it is an economic space similar in function to the territory of a single state. the white paper on the creation of a single (internal) market presented by the european commission in 1985 was the first to mention the creation of an internal market. the adoption of the single european act, the most important provision of which was the decision to gradually complete the internal market by the end of 1992, was crucial to the full realisation of the internal market. the aim of the european union's single market is to achieve four principles: • free movement of goods • free movement of services • free movement of persons • free movement of capital. the free movement of goods (both industrial and agricultural) was conditional on the abolition of customs duties and all similar charges between eu countries. it was also necessary to establish a common customs tariff for trade with countries outside the union.
in writing. − i regret that we are once again forced to speak out on an issue as fundamental as the equality of eu citizens, their right to free movement and residence. i am even more concerned that our debate is the consequence of a debate that has its roots in highly developed countries that boast a deeply rooted democratic tradition. today's resolution calls on member states to respect and monitor the right to free movement of persons within the eu. this right must not be infringed under any circumstances and any citizen working in any member state of the european union other than his country of origin must be able to enjoy the same social rights as his fellow workers. let us not forget that the european union was created for the benefit of its citizens, and their mobility is one of the greatest achievements of its architects. we, as members of the european parliament, therefore have a duty to react and protect citizens against attempts to introduce mechanisms which discriminate against them and restrict their freedoms.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the sale of eu citizenship. the concept that eu citizenship can be bought is a very bad idea, because it divides people into better and worse people based on their wealth. it is no secret that wealthy individuals who buy citizenship of another country often do so because of problems with the justice system of their country of origin or residence. malta has the full right to set its own rules, but maltese citizenship also entitles you to hold an eu passport. such practices may undermine the principle of free movement of persons, which is one of the eu's fundamental principles. the maltese authorities should consider whether the proposed solution would cause more harm than good.
in writing. - malta's actions have sparked a heated debate on the sale of citizenship by eu countries. the resolution we have voted today calls on the european commission to examine whether such measures, whether direct or indirect, are in any way compatible with the spirit of the treaties. it should be noted that we cannot treat eu citizenship as a commodity, but rather as a privilege. moreover, eu citizenship cannot be based on economic criteria - someone can afford it, so he or she buys it; the foundation of this citizenship should be a sense of community, which i believe is lacking in some decision-makers.
in writing. - i supported the resolution on eu citizenship for sale, which criticises the concept of trading eu citizenship. while member states have exclusive competence in matters of nationality and citizenship, decisions on these matters directly affect other member states and their citizens. the granting of citizenship of one of the countries of the union automatically confers rights of free movement and residence in the territory of the other member states. the acquisition of citizenship is also contrary to the principle of non-discrimination, as only the wealthiest third-country nationals can make such a purchase. in my view, the concept of 'economic citizenship' is also incompatible with the very idea of citizenship, which traditionally implies a permanent link with the state and the rights and obligations that follow from this fact.
in writing. - it has not been this easy to become a citizen of the union for decades. but there's a catch: it's a gateway to the rich. europe is a fortress under siege, defending its borders with all its might against immigrants, poor africans and asians who often pay the price of their lives to reach the shores of lampedusa in broken-down boats. but europe is opening its doors to wealthy immigrants, making it easier for them to settle permanently wherever possible. and many countries do, from austria to the united kingdom.

in writing. − the new icelandic government has suspended the accession negotiations, which have been ongoing since july 2010, until a national referendum on joining the european union has been held. the public is divided on this issue, and the new authorities have rightly decided that such an important decision about the future of their country should be in the hands of the citizens. in a report adopted today, the european parliament takes note of the government's position and awaits the outcome of the referendum. as i fully support the right of each country to be able to make sovereign decisions, especially on such an important issue as eu accession, i voted with the ecr group in favour of this report.
in writing. − during the several years of eu accession negotiations with iceland, the country made the changes required in this process. in addition to issues such as financial services, food security and capital flows, which require further attention from the authorities, overall progress in the european economic area should be considered satisfactory. although iceland is in many ways an attractive potential member of the union, the accession process was halted last year. however, contact has not been frozen, although cooperation and the increased compatibility of the two systems would certainly have proceeded much more rapidly if the exchange of information and practices under the programmes in place in connection with the accession process had continued. iceland's earlier accession efforts in 2010 were a strategic decision with long-term implications and prospects, and it is to be hoped that the continued vigorous policy of enlarging the union's borders to include more countries will once again encourage the icelandic authorities to resume negotiations. the benefits for both parties would be to facilitate basic cooperation, enhance development prospects and increase the stability of political and economic relations.

in writing. − on 16 january 2014, the european parliament adopted a resolution on an eu strategy for the homeless. as homelessness is the most extreme form of poverty, tackling it has become a priority in the europe 2020 strategy initiative european platform for cooperation against poverty and social exclusion. in the plenary vote i supported the adoption of the resolution because it calls for immediate action to combat poverty. calls on the european commission to develop a strategy to combat homelessness without delay, with the long-term objective of putting an end to homelessness;
in writing. − as a result of the economic and financial crisis, the problem of homelessness has affected many eu member states on an unprecedented scale in recent years. although homelessness has become a priority of the eu's poverty reduction policy under the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to reduce the number of people living in poverty and at risk of social exclusion by at least 20 million, it remains a major social problem. it is therefore necessary to develop without delay a union strategy to tackle homelessness, in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity, which would play a supporting and complementary role to the comprehensive actions undertaken by member states at national, regional and local level, in particular those concerning housing, preventive strategies to reduce evictions and cooperation with relevant aid organisations providing support, counselling and guidance to homeless people. i voted against the criminalization of homelessness that is happening in some countries. poor material conditions should not be penalized and member states should focus on helping and creating opportunities for those affected by poverty.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy aims to reduce the number of people living in poverty and social exclusion by 20 million by 2020. however, homelessness is not only an extreme form of social exclusion, but also a situation from which self-management and reintegration are significantly hampered. it is also worrying that since 2008 the problem of homelessness in the eu has become more acute. citizens affected by extreme poverty or homelessness are unable to fulfil their potential or to take effective care of themselves and their loved ones. they are also more prone to health problems, aggression, and various forms of addiction and malnutrition. their significantly reduced level of participation in the institutions of social life effectively limits their ability to exercise even their basic rights. especially dangerous to society is the growing number of families with children living in poverty and homelessness. children growing up in such conditions are not only exposed to a number of dangers, but their connections with society are damaged from an early age, which can result in the wasting of lives and the potential of many valuable individuals. the eu should continue to support the actions of national governments, in particular in terms of data exchange, experience of trends and effective remedies. the key principle here should be to identify the causes and effectively address the situations that lead to poverty and homelessness.
in writing. − the text of the resolution stressed that homelessness constitutes a violation of fundamental human rights and therefore needs to be addressed. as this phenomenon has increased significantly in many member states in recent years, the document calls for an integrated union strategy. it calls for the use of european funds to combat homelessness and for the establishment of measurable rules to monitor member states' progress in combating the phenomenon. it also calls for a comprehensive research programme to build knowledge and exchange experience in tackling homelessness as part of the eu strategy to combat homelessness. building on national and regional strategies, the eu strategy would end street homelessness by 2015.

in writing. the free movement of persons is fundamental to the functioning of the european union. unfortunately, as the report under consideration points out, in many cases it is precisely because of the change of residence that union citizens, when dealing with the various institutions of the state in which they intend to settle, are obliged to comply with certain formal requirements and to produce documents issued in another member state in this connection. this often entails the need to incur significant financial costs associated with the legalisation, authentication and translation of documents. the simplification of crossborder red tape and the introduction of multilingual official forms recognised in all community countries is therefore a step in the right direction. the proposed catalogue of cases in which multilingual forms would be issued does not interfere with the scope of the substantive law in force in each country. it relates only to the certification of facts, legal acts and legal status of natural persons, without imposing any obligation to recognise their content. the introduction of these will therefore undoubtedly reduce bureaucracy and make it easier for union citizens to function in a united europe.

the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? the draft report i am presenting to you today is a response to the european commission's eu justice scoreboard. the commission's communication itself has caused a lot of excitement both in the european parliament and among the member states, so i would like to explain once again what exactly is already wrapped in the legend of the justice scoreboard. it is more or less a compilation of various indicators providing an overview of the efficiency and effectiveness of the judicial system in the member states in the area of civil, commercial and administrative law. the scoreboard is therefore by no means a ranking of quality. it cannot be treated and seen as a political instrument either. i therefore fully agree with the commission's assumption, which was the basis for this document, that an effective and independent judicial system and predictable, timely and enforceable judgments are important elements of an attractive business environment that positively affects market development and investment growth. in addition, the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance. the european commission has made a useful exercise, but i would like to draw attention to one essential point. the comparison of national judicial systems must be based on objective criteria and data which are objectively collected, comparable and analysable, which is unfortunately not easy in practice. in my report i draw particular attention to a number of problems which arise from the analysis of the commission document. in my view, there was a lack of broader information on crossborder cases, which are often more complex, more complicated than national proceedings. such data would allow us to identify the remaining obstacles that citizens face in exercising their rights under the eu's single market. i also draw attention to the importance of alternative dispute resolution methods in reducing the burden on judicial systems and the costs for all parties concerned. i would also like to point out once again the absolutely crucial issue of training judicial staff in both knowledge of eu legislation and existing legal instruments and knowledge of foreign languages. a very interesting category presented by the commission was the use of new technologies in communication and case resolution. the differences between member states are enormous in this respect. i think we should encourage the use of ict because it can significantly reduce costs and speed up court proceedings. in conclusion, i would like to emphasise once again that the justice scoreboard is primarily intended to highlight good practices and trends that member states can adopt to increase the effectiveness of their legal systems. however, i would be very careful not to go in the direction of a harsh assessment of individual judicial systems, as that is not the intention behind this initiative. the same applies to the extension of the scoreboard to areas outside the european union's competence. i am sure that this kind of action can only discourage and discourage member states from taking any action, because such an analysis is directed precisely, or perhaps even specifically, to member states so that they can consider it.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? i'm not going to let you do this. ladies and gentlemen! the problems of small farms require a broader approach. first, to create the conditions for the maintenance and development of agricultural production. secondly, in support of alternative sources of income, their diversification through the development of services, non-agricultural production or the taking up of work outside the farm. third, the production of public goods for the environment, the maintenance of the landscape or biodiversity requires the creation of a system of valuation of these activities and the establishment of forms of payment for these products. the production functions of small farms are largely limited to self-sufficiency and are characterised by a low link with the market. it's important to produce these public goods. but i want to draw attention to the unique function of this agriculture in terms of jobs that it provides for millions of people. these farms are a reservoir of labour. on the one hand, when the economy shrinks, they take in this surplus labor. when an economy grows, that surplus labor is diverted from itself to the economy. secondly, these farms reduce rural exclusion and poverty. finally, these farms are steeped in tradition, regional, local culture and folk customs. they are the place where local and regional products are made. we're seeing a systematic depopulation of the countryside. to counteract this, it is necessary to create good, sustainable prospects for this group of farms, including in the area of agricultural production, as well as the possibility of obtaining additional sources of income outside agriculture, as i have already mentioned. the reform of the common agricultural policy has started this process. farms up to 10 hectares are exempt from crop diversification, up to 15 hectares do not have to exclude the so-called ecological area. the reform simplifies the system of submission of applications and controls in these holdings. member states have the possibility to support this group of farms under the rural development programmes, the so-called second pillar. significant opportunities for entrepreneurship and job creation by persons associated with these holdings exist under other union programmes. in addition, assistance of a social and welfare nature may also be directed to these holdings under the european social fund. there are also possibilities to support these farms through national programmes, i.e. financed from national budgets. we need to do more to strengthen the action, the openness, the determination to develop entrepreneurship by people in the small farming sector. in conclusion, small farms are a boon, but they are also a problem. they are a benefit because they provide self-sufficiency, they provide self-employment, they have a positive impact on the environment, the landscape, they keep difficult areas alive, especially mountainous areas and the like. they are a problem because it is difficult to earn enough to support a family. so they're not very competitive, they're much more expensive to produce because of higher fixed costs, lack of investment and development resources, technologies are outdated. finally, i would like to point out the need to create the conditions for the development of production based on own raw materials on the farm. it's about local, regional products that would be sold in the local market as part of this short food chain. many changes are required in the areas of taxation, insurance, and control and compliance. it is generally a matter of simplifying, of creating more opportunities for the development of different production, different forms of processing on the small farms, in order to ensure them an adequate level of income.
in writing. some small farms have highly efficient, technologically advanced or labour-intensive production, which generates a decent income for the owners. however, most small farms do not have such facilities. with little access to the market, producing mainly for self-sufficiency, they fulfil socio-cultural functions, providing certain public goods of a natural and landscape nature. such farms are the only alternative to unemployment for the owners. in addition to the cap, other eu policies need to be integrated to address the problems of small farms, which are of varying intensity across europe, to finance social and welfare measures, but also education, training and the creation of alternative jobs. it should be possible to apply national measures of the member states in this respect, with the agreement of the ec, of course.

mr. chairman, please! after months of negotiations, we are today adopting the final version of the directive on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation. i have no doubt that this is a finished product and a great example of precision regulation that dynamically adapts to new threats that arise in financial markets. in this context, it is worth recalling once again that the econ committee has made this clear and has unanimously supported the report by mrs mccarthy. the free movement of financial services in conditions of free competition is one of the major achievements of european integration. however, the fair competition underpinning the free market economy and private law presupposes equality of opportunity, and this has often been distorted by unfair market participants who have been allowed to go unpunished. the scale of the potential distortions was illustrated by the libor scandal, which manipulated $350 trillion in financial instruments. with this package, we are creating what appears to be an effective tool to reduce this information asymmetry, which not only poses a threat to security and trust in trade, but also generates suboptimal allocation. in the course of the econ committee's work, we have succeeded, among other things, in clarifying the scope of the regulation in question by clearly indicating which financial instruments may be affected by the infringement. we have managed to harmonize the definition with mifid, to introduce a new category of crime, namely improper disclosure of confidential information, or finally (which seems to me personally a breakthrough) to harmonize the penalty level of 2 and 4 years of imprisonment for the most serious violations in the use and disclosure of confidential information. the aim of the directive is to enhance investor confidence and ensure market integrity for all of us by prohibiting persons with inside information from trading in the financial instruments to which that information relates and by prohibiting market manipulation. the fraud regulation is a good example of the application of the new article 83 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which allows for the introduction of criminal sanctions to ensure the effectiveness of the european union's policy in such a sensitive area. at the same time, i believe that in the case of financial market manipulation, the threat of prison seems to be the most effective deterrent. i shall therefore vote in favour of this report and once again i would like to offer my warmest congratulations to mrs mccarthy.

in writing. - the international convention on the safety of fishing vessels, adopted in 1997 at the torremolinos conference, was the first international instrument on the safety of fishing vessels. the convention contains safety requirements for new, offshore fishing vessels of 24 metres in length and above. the ten chapters of the annex to the torremolinos convention concern the construction and fitting out of machinery, electrical installations, fire protection, protection of crews, life-saving equipment, radiotelegraphy and radiotelephony and navigational equipment. the torremolinos protocol of 1999 complements the convention, taking into account technological developments in recent years and the need to provide a reasonable incentive for the ratification of this international legal instrument. the protocol arrangements shall cover unattended machinery spaces, enhanced life-saving measures, life-jackets and thermal protection measures, communication systems and other elements of the gmdss. council directive 97/70/ec of 11 december 1997 establishes the safety standards for tower mills in the countries of the european union.

in writing. - the report adopted today on promoting free movement by simplifying the acceptance of certain official documents is of great importance to the citizens of the european union. freedom of movement and employment have enabled many europeans to live or stay temporarily, for example for study, work or simply for leisure, in an eu member state other than their own. all these people may have contact with the administration of the member state in which they are staying, either on tax or social security matters, or as students with the administration of a university, and a number of bureaucratic barriers may arise. the administration may require a certified translation of documents or an apostille, and this not only involves a great deal of effort but also costs for citizens. these issues are of fundamental importance for the internal market as they affect the practical functioning of the fundamental freedoms of the union. administrative formalities discourage many citizens from moving to another member state. i supported the report because, by abolishing the additional formalities required in crossborder situations, it is an important step towards making it easier for citizens to enjoy the freedom of movement to which they are entitled.
in writing. - europe has become mobile. the principle of free movement of persons works well, allowing our citizens to work, study or simply move to any of the member states. this is undoubtedly a merit of the european union fulfilling its most important objectives, and as a member of the european parliament i am extremely proud of this achievement. through this cultural exchange, we broaden our horizons: not only do we learn about the customs and ways of life of other nations, but we also learn new ways of solving problems, we see many things from a completely different perspective and sooner or later we see how much benefit such an exchange of experience can bring. it is therefore of the utmost importance that europeans have as little difficulty as possible with the administrative procedures necessary to enjoy a comfortable stay abroad, whether for business, study or tourism. this report proposes, inter alia, the introduction of universal, multilingual forms to facilitate administrative procedures of an international nature and suggests some solutions to the issue of acceptance of documents translated in a country other than the one where they are submitted. the author also wants to reduce costs for both stakeholders and administrative bodies, as well as to reduce the amount of potential fraud and to promote mutual trust.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the rapkaya report because i consider it an important step towards facilitating and eliminating unnecessary formalities in the free movement of persons. this issue concerns the many millions of union citizens who reside or stay temporarily in a member state other than their own. for these people, administrative barriers, which are complex and often costly, often discourage them from settling or doing business abroad. i realise that this is a complex issue and not all the changes proposed can be implemented overnight, but i think this report is quite balanced and reasonable. i agree with the rapporteur that the principle of mutual trust should apply in the common internal market and that copies certified as being in conformity with the original made in one member state should therefore remain valid in all community countries. i also consider it justified to accept uncertified translations and, if necessary, to prepare a certified translation, the costs of which should be borne by the requesting authority.
in writing. - the free movement of persons is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union. one of the greatest obstacles to this freedom is the excessive bureaucracy faced by citizens and businesses. this bureaucracy is manifested in the excessively stringent conditions to which the individual documents required to be produced for the purpose of dealing with a particular case must meet. this is contrary not only to the principle of free movement of citizens but also to the principle of freedom to conduct economic activities, which in turn has a major impact on the free movement of capital, services and labour. excessive restrictions therefore undermine the fundamental freedoms that are the foundation of the european union's free market. the introduction of legislation liberalising the requirements for receiving certain official documents will unlock this freedom and will undoubtedly reduce the waiting time for citizens to deal with specific matters.
in writing. - according to the latest eurostat data, in 2011, some 12 million european citizens were living in a member state other than their country of origin. these figures are then added to the equally important numbers of people living abroad within the eu for a limited period of time, such as students or workers. following the guidance published by the commission in a strategy paper highlighting the main criticisms of the internal market raised by citizens and businesses, most of these were directed at administrative and bureaucratic difficulties. i therefore believe that today's vote, which aims to simplify administrative procedures and the acceptance of certain public documents, is a decisive step towards making life easier for millions of european citizens who often have to deal with the bureaucracy of an eu country other than their own.
in writing. - the draft regulation aims to reduce formalities and make it easier for citizens who frequently cross the border. today, a large number of eu citizens live in a member state other than their own, and the number is growing. often, the administrative formalities are very complicated. citizens may have documents legalised by the authorities of one member state, but still be required to pay for sworn translations or for the production of certified copies of official documents. the needs of citizens, not government officials, are paramount, and we should continue to work to improve the free movement of people and reduce red tape.
in writing. - the report calls for the abolition of some of the existing formalities, which is in the interest of citizens and the economy of europe as a whole. this is particularly important for some polish citizens and entrepreneurs who are abroad in other eu countries and face difficulties in understanding the administrative situation in their country and incur additional costs through the translation of documents. the abolition of additional formalities for certain official documents, such as certified translations or legalization through diplomatic channels, will undoubtedly benefit union citizens. the authentication and translation of documents such as certificates of education and civil status certificates recognised in each eu country is one of a number of proposals that will help to eliminate administrative problems and speed up official procedures. modernising member states' administrations and administrative cooperation and reducing widespread suspicion of union citizens by shifting the translation burden from the applicant to the authority concerned will go a long way towards eliminating excessive bureaucracy and introducing the principle of mutual trust, while introducing multilingual eu standard forms will make life easier for citizens and businesses operating across borders. in view of the above, i shall vote in favour of the report on promoting the free movement of citizens and businesses by simplifying the acceptance of certain official documents in the european union.
in writing. - the european commission has taken another step towards reducing the administrative burden on citizens and businesses. currently, the formalities to be completed to register official documents, such as a birth certificate, in another eu member state are too much. citizens who move to another eu country have to spend a lot of time and money to prove that official documents (such as birth certificates or marriage certificates) issued in their home country are authentic. this also applies to the so-called apostille seal (otherwise known as the apostille clause), which is issued by a public authority as proof that an official document or the signature of an official on a document is authentic. for example, they often have to provide a variety of official documents certifying their legal status when operating in another country. these requirements date back to a time when a country only recognized official documents that were issued by the foreign ministry of another country. however, just as we recognise national court judgments, we should be able to trust the civil registry office of another eu country that issues the birth certificate, without the need for a guarantee from the relevant ministry of foreign affairs, ministry of justice or other authority. the european commission has therefore today proposed to remove the apostille stamp and other confusing administrative requirements for the certification of official documents that apply to people living and working in other member states.

in writing. - information on the hazards of chemicals is provided by means of standard warnings and pictograms on labels and in safety data sheets. the new terms replaced the previously used wording: • mixtures instead of preparations • hazardous instead of dangerous • pictograms instead of symbols • hazard statements instead of r statements indicating the nature of the risk • precautionary statements instead of s statements indicating the conditions of safe use • warning words (e. g. danger, caution) have replaced the hazard statements. the new red-framed pictograms are gradually replacing the familiar orange warning symbols. in most cases, the decision on the classification of a substance or mixture is taken by the supplier. this is called self-classification. in some cases, the decision on the classification of a chemical is taken at community level to ensure appropriate risk management. this applies in general to the most dangerous substances: carcinogens, mutagens or substances with harmful effects on reproduction, substances with allergic effects on the respiratory tract, biocidal products or plant protection products. all previous harmonised classifications of substances drawn up under previously applicable legislation (the dangerous substances directive) have been converted to clp harmonised classifications. suppliers shall be obliged to apply this harmonised classification and labelling.

in writing. - in many eu member states people from lgbti groups face daily discrimination, harassment and prejudice across all areas of social and economic life. misconceptions about homosexuality and transgender persons further fuel intolerant attitudes and behaviour towards this community, making it more vulnerable to verbal and physical attacks. aiming to tackle this reality, the european parliament requested in the past years to develop a roadmap for equality for lgbti. the current report builds on these appeals. the report calls on the commission to make proposals for addressing non-discrimination of lgbti in employment, education and health in the field of citizenship, families, free movement, freedom of assembly and expression. although this report faced a degree of hostility from conservative groups, its core provisions respect the principle of subsidiarity, and they rely on existing eu policies and frameworks. accordingly the report recommends that these tools be made available and apply equally to lgbti persons. i believe that lgbti persons deserve to be treated with the same degree of respect and dignity as any other citizens in the ue. this report is a positive step towards achieving this goal.
in writing. - the european parliament came up with another document which not only blatantly violates subsidiarity, but is itself a pathetic illustration of ideological fanaticism. homophobia is a stick with which today’s fanatics beat everyone who dares to disagree with them. there is no greater nonsense than to claim that homosexuals are victimised. the opposite is true. they are the most privileged group today. the homosexual radicals are becoming increasingly radical because they can get away with anything. the lesbian hoodlums physically attacked the belgian archbishop in the university of brussels; the scholars who raise even the slightest doubts about this lamentable institution called homosexual marriage are bullied and harassed. the list of such disgraceful actions is long and gets longer every day. the european parliament should speak in defence of the real victims, and not become an accomplice of the victimisers.
in writing. - as a member of the european parliament, i support all actions to combat homophobia and discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. i voted against the report by mrs ulrike lunacek. the main reason for my decision was the formal context of this report. it contains provisions which are in clear contradiction with the principle of subsidiarity. this principle governs both eu and member state competences, i.e. it allows the eu to intervene only when the lisbon treaty so provides the remaining issues are the exclusive competence of national parliaments and member state governments. in practice, the lunacek report is an attempt to force member states, such as poland, to recognise same-sex partnerships or marriages and their consequences, when such do not yet exist in our country's legal order (e.g. same-sex partnerships, same-sex marriages, adoption of children by same-sex couples, etc.). the question of introducing a partnership institution in poland is the exclusive competence of the polish constitutional institutions and not of the european parliament. i would also like to emphasise that i am a strong supporter of equality and the protection of the fundamental rights of eu citizens. for this reason, i cannot agree with the provisions of the resolution on positive discrimination against any social group, for example in the field of health care. i stress that all citizens, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, etc., should have equal access to health care or other services.
in writing. - the adoption of the document by the ep will in practice mean a wide range of rights for the minority, but unfortunately also restrictions for the majority. this project will give homosexuals a privileged position in the labour market, as sexual orientation can become a decisive criterion for employment. for example, if an employer does not hire a gay person, he may be a 'homophobic criminal'. the lunacek report commits the european commission to the most vocal lgbt community demands for guidelines that will force eu member states to respect the right to family reunification so that all forms of family life are legally recognized in national laws. this means that civil partnerships and marriages, even those concluded outside the country, are recognised in all eu countries. the same will be true of legal gender recognition. after the lgbt lobby is satisfied with the outcome of the vote on the report, there will be no obstacles to gay marriage and gender selection. it seems that among the sexual minority there is another minority - the lgbt elite - a handful of people who want to decide everything and for everyone. a minority that intends to take away the rights of the majority and become a group with exceptional opportunities, with a wide range of privileges.
in writing. - mr. president, i'm not going to let you do this. unfair practices by traders are a nuisance to consumers. in particular in the new member states, where the rules on protection of transactions still leave much to be desired, traders have been using clearly misleading methods for years. misguided advertising is often used, such as the publication of inaccurate information in brochures and catalogues. the potential of this directive should be fully exploited in order to increase consumer confidence in transactions on european markets. in this respect, i agree with the principle of disciplining countries which continue to violate it. it also appears necessary to strengthen cooperation between national institutions responsible for protecting consumer rights. i hope this will improve the efficiency and reduce the cost of the claims.
in writing. - i believe that in an era of increasing digitalisation and dominance of online shopping, we need to look more closely at the rules ensuring that consumers' rights are protected when they transact in the internal market. increasingly, unfair commercial practices are found on forums, social networks and blogs, where messages of an advertising nature are hidden in the form of comments. member states should therefore warn consumers against all forms of unfair practices by organising information campaigns and by publicising fraud in the media. the success of this is dependent on the uniform enforcement of the directive in all member states, which has unfortunately not been uniformly observed by all member states. in order to ensure that consumers are effectively assisted in the exercise of their rights, member states must also implement the directive on alternative dispute resolution and online out-of-court dispute resolution. i think it is also very important to strengthen the role of consumer organisations and to strengthen the cooperation of these associations with the relevant national authorities responsible for implementing the directive.
in writing. - the unfair commercial practices directive has been in force for several years now, and there is no need to amend it at present, but the correct implementation of this directive into national legal systems is crucial. after these few years of application of the directive, it has become clear that some very onerous commercial practices still exist in the single market. the elimination of those practices is important to increase consumer confidence in transactions on the market and to provide businesses with a higher level of legal certainty. among the misleading marketing practices that cause the most problems for businesses in europe, the issue of dishonest companies offering business directory listings seems particularly worrying. such a listing in business directories is often combined with a form that dishonest companies send out, asking businesses to update information in their business directories, ostensibly free of charge. if the undertakings concerned sign such a form, they are informed that they have signed the contract and will be charged for the costs. i supported the report because it calls, among other things, for the elimination of such practices. the scale of the problem is shown by the figures: over 13 000 complaints from 16 different member states were documented. the smes sector is the most exposed to such practices and the report is therefore an important step towards better implementation of the directive.
in writing. - unfair trading practices are one of the most important obstacles to competition in the european union market. it should be noted that many practices considered unfair and distorting competition have been prohibited at union level. the most important is the prohibition of the sale of products that are not allowed to be legally marketed. the largest group of unfair commercial practices that undermine competition and fair trade are marketing activities involving the use of various forms of consumer awareness raising in advertising. this is particularly true of sub-threshold advertising and advertising that appeals to fear and other emotions. it was therefore of the utmost importance to harmonise the definitions of unfair commercial practices and misleading practices, which differed from one member state to another before the entry into force of the directive.
in writing. - previous attempts at eu harmonisation of the law on unfair competition by means of directives have concerned issues that are at the margins of this area of law (e.g. misleading advertising, advertising in electronic commerce, etc.). however, the multiplicity of regulations on specific consumer protection issues did not, in the view of the european legislator, promote a sense of legal certainty for both consumers and traders, who, in their activities on eu territory, had to take account of the different regulations on commercial practices in the various member states of the community.
in writing. - in march 2013, the european commission published a communication presenting the eu justice scoreboard, a non-binding benchmarking tool designed to present the long-term trends observed in the functioning of national justice systems. it is a tool whose scope is to be gradually increased in terms of areas covered, as well as indicators and methodologies. the commission emphasises that the scope of the table covers those elements of the justice system which contribute to improving the business and investment climate, and thus relates in particular to civil and commercial and administrative (not criminal) procedural matters, thus falling within the framework of the european semester, the europe 2020 strategy, the strengthening of the single market and the eu action programme for citizens. the scoreboard was based on indicators such as length of proceedings, number of pending cases, ict systems for courts, alternative dispute resolution and training of judges.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the impact of the development of smart grids at local and regional level. they are the result of intensive technological progress in the information and communication sector and the desire of individual regions to ensure a stable energy supply while maintaining sustainable development. investments in the development of smart grids in the union bring a number of benefits, such as lower energy prices, increased share of renewable energy, reduced greenhouse gas emissions and development of the research and innovation sector. the use of these energy networks is particularly important in disadvantaged regions and island areas where they can bring significant economic benefits and ensure security of energy supply. moreover, the efficiency of these systems will be enhanced if we link their development to the housing, transport, environment and spatial planning sectors. i believe that investing in smart energy systems in individual regions of europe will guarantee the security of energy supply to individual households, while making more efficient use of it for local needs, and at the same time will contribute to the creation of many new jobs.
in writing. - in the coming years, eu regions will have to find a way to ensure a stable, affordable and secure energy supply. in an era of rising energy prices and a world facing climate change, the challenge of establishing a reliable energy supply system is a major one. in the new financial perspective 2014-2020, we will focus on supporting the energy market transformation with a view to achieving a low-carbon economy in all sectors, using cohesion policy funds. as this is only the beginning of the great process of deploying smart grids in europe, it is necessary to develop a balanced action plan. a large-scale information and promotion campaign to encourage the public to use renewable energy sources will play an important role, including by educating eu citizens on how to use the lowest possible prices and save energy while improving efficiency. smart grids mean security of energy supply and a significant reduction in dependence on fossil fuels, as well as the creation of new jobs. the key to their effective implementation in each eu region will be openness and transparency in the relationships between local authorities, businesses, industry and citizens, so that they can reach the remote and poor areas of europe. the experience gained over the years has shown that this type of synergy brings much greater and longer-term benefits to the regions. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. - intelligent networks are essential to solving today's problems. aging infrastructure and increased demand are making the system inefficient. therefore, cooperation initiatives in all fields should be pursued to create modern smart grids to reverse this trend. but without local solutions, europe cannot cope with this challenge. it should not be forgotten that the networks must also be a source of information on the level of consumption, the range of efficiency. we have little time left, and that is why we need to make key decisions for the next decade.

in writing. - it is very important that the european parliament has adopted a report on the future of small farms. it is the first such document in which parliament has fully addressed this important sector in agriculture and the countryside. in the eu, two thirds of farms have less than 5 ha of arable land. the non-productive functions of these farms are important. they are more environmentally friendly, contribute to the maintenance of the landscape and biodiversity. they also provide jobs for many millions of people and play a significant role in maintaining local traditions and customs and in producing regional products. it is important to highlight the marked differences in the situation of these farms not only in the so-called old and new union, but also within individual countries. small farms that benefit from cap support have been better organised for decades, forming producer groups, various associations, have different forms of processing, are also better equipped and more connected to the market, which increases their competitiveness and profitability. in contrast, small farms in countries that have joined the eu in recent years are technically under-resourced, production-oriented, self-sufficient, poorly organised in producer groups and little connected to the market. they are mainly social. moreover, some of these farms exist without the necessary economic infrastructure. forms of support for this group of holdings must therefore be diversified.

today, we pay almost twice as much for electricity in europe as we do in the united states. of course, partly because of taxes, partly because of para-taxation, but climate policy has a very important role to play here. the most advanced renewable technologies today can replace, eliminate, a ton of co2 emissions in electricity production at a cost of 200 euros. other technologies, such as photovoltaics or offshore wind, cost between 500 and 900 euros per tonne of co2 emissions. it's not well-spent money. it's just too expensive. and then there's the environmental costs, which we don't like to talk about. the environmental costs of such a policy are very obvious. this energy - renewable energy - is volatile, it's unpredictable, so there's a conventional power plant somewhere in the back that has to be running all the time. very often in european conditions, they're coal-fired power plants. very often, these coal-fired power plants are just working to send electricity through the air. i don't think there's a worse model, from an environmental standpoint, and also from a business standpoint, than to produce energy just in case. our energy and climate package was designed to ensure our sustainable development, to ensure our energy security, and ultimately to ensure the competitiveness of our economy. that balance has been broken today in favor of environmental goals. today we have an opportunity, a chance to restore that balance. if we want to restore this balance, this policy must be based on a single objective: a realistically defined objective, correlated with international agreements. this policy must be flexible for both countries and sectors of the economy; finally, this policy must be a policy of low energy prices. otherwise, the balance between business and environmental objectives will continue to be broken. otherwise, the vitality of the european economy will not be restored, and today it is very much needed. unfortunately, without any substantial changes in this report, this text does not meet these challenges. this text is even much less constructive than the commission's proposals. without any substantial changes to this report, i will encourage you to reject this report.

in writing. we argue on the a priori assumption that anthropogenic co2 emissions are the main culprit of climate change. no one has ever proved this hypothesis, and its endorsement as "faith" is dogmatic. i regard the ipcc experience as a 'throwing of the dice'". i'm not arguing with the commission, which believes the ipcc. faith is hard to argue with. however, assuming that it contains some rational premise, i would point out that: first, the eu's ambition concerns about 10% of global co2 emissions and reducing it will not affect the climate. even assuming that the ipcc is correct, the insistence on plans for 2030 and beyond is reckless, cynical or foolish for those who insist on doing so at the expense of the european economy and its competitiveness; secondly, the alternative to the current energy model imposed on member states in the form of a single-unit paradigm for distributed renewable energy is unrealistic and irrational. the authors of this proposal make a methodological error, because renewable energy in europe is unevenly distributed; thirdly, the european emissions trading system as a purported market tool does not meet the intended objectives. it ignores the role of agriculture and forestry in actively reducing the emissions of a gas that is essential to life on our planet. on the contrary, it leads to global deforestation and reduced food production.

in writing. the report under discussion is a de facto enhanced protection of airline passengers' rights. the proposed regulation would give every passenger the right to compensation when their flight is cancelled or delayed. the establishment of specific procedures for the conditions and manner of payment of compensation will facilitate and streamline the movement of passengers. the most common complaint by passengers so far is that their rights are ignored by airlines using the term 'extraordinary circumstances'. therefore, a precise definition of this term would remove any ambiguity in the payment of compensation. a very important aspect for each customer is to specify the definition of the 'ticket price' which contains all the basic information, i.e. the issue of the boarding pass, the minimum baggage allowance and the credit card fee. passengers will have the right to be informed of any other costs before the booking process begins. you will be allowed to bring on board, without any additional charge, your personal belongings as well as goods purchased at the airport. the creation of dedicated baggage claim points and the availability of a standardised complaint form in all the languages of the european union will ensure that passengers are able to resolve their inconvenience quickly and without any problems. another very important issue will be the prohibition of cancellation of a return flight if the passenger does not take the flight tam , i.e. the first leg of the journey. some of the changes are beneficial to passengers, and some are beneficial to carriers. in the end, i think the interests of both parties have been rationally balanced.
