in writing. - on tuesday 4 february 2014, the european parliament voted on a report on illegal female migrants in the european union. the report raises the alarm about the plight of women who are in the eu but do not have documents. it emphasises that the group of illegal immigrant women is a social group particularly vulnerable to trafficking, discrimination and exploitation in the labour market. migrant women from third countries (without documents) are also exposed to double and sometimes triple discrimination: on the basis of gender, legal status and sometimes skin colour. it therefore encourages member states to provide psychological support, health care and legal assistance to illegal migrants and to take appropriate steps to prevent the spread of prostitution and forced labour among this social group. i voted for the report, which is about defending the most vulnerable, the most disenfranchised.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on undocumented women migrants in the european union (2013/2115(ini)). this report is more than just a matter of population, immigration laws and employment. what this document offers is the protection of fundamental human rights. as eu citizens we have the luxury of health care, education and protection from prosecution, and this report enforces those standards for migrant women. as was stated in the report, ‘the recommendations proposed in the report focus on three main points. the first point encourages the member states to uncouple immigration policies from health care, education and the prosecution of crimes against undocumented migrants. access to basic health care, education and protection of physical integrity are fundamental rights, and undocumented migrants are entitled to them, despite their residential or legal status. so, migrants should be able to access these basic services and also report abusers to the police without fearing arrest and deportation’. furthermore, one must bear in mind that the people who come to the eu view it as an opportunity to provide better for their families and are mostly law-abiding citizens who are often pushed to the outer fringes of society due to their situation or ethnicity.
in writing. - it is estimated that there are between 2 and 4 million illegal migrants in the european union. through poverty and poor working conditions, they put their own health and that of others at risk, for example by spreading untreated infections. illegal migrants face a number of legal, economic and practical challenges along the way. access to healthcare is a basic human right, but eu member states are not obliged to provide it to migrants on the same terms as citizens. the minimum should be ensured especially for children and pregnant and postpartum women. another problem faced by illegal immigrants is the skyrocketing cost of medical care. this is particularly true for groups at particular risk, such as pregnant women, who have access to medical care in each of the countries studied, but only in belgium, france, italy and greece is it completely free. only in two countries - spain and greece - do children of illegal migrants have access to medical care on the same terms as children of their own nationals.
in writing. - the lack of interest among eu citizens in taking up seasonal work in the tourist, agricultural or horticultural sectors is increasingly prompting european employers to hire non-eu nationals. the adoption of a package of legislative procedures with today's directive will help to prevent the exploitation of third-country workers. it will also ensure equal working conditions, legal protection and the conditions and duration of residence and work permits. another benefit of this directive is the introduction of simplifications in the entry procedure for third-country nationals who seek employment in the union on the basis of a contract of employment or a binding offer of employment which specifies the amount of remuneration. the provisions also specify the maximum period of employment for seasonal workers, which is six months, and require the employer to provide accommodation for seasonal workers. i believe that, in accordance with the treaty, the union must develop a migration policy aimed at ensuring equal respect for and enforcement of rights vis-à-vis third-country nationals, which will help to minimise the wave of illegal immigration.
in writing. - with good wages and a high standard of living, a part of european society does not want to do low-paid, often exhausting seasonal work. these are usually agricultural work at harvest or employment in services. unfortunately, such wages are often poor, and working conditions and hygiene are not up to par. incidents of detention, exploitation and discrimination against workers are also worth mentioning. to stop illegal labour migration, it is necessary to create rules that restrict this practice. it is about regulating the legal system between employers and employees, which makes it easy to hire and work under fair conditions. i also fully agree with the inclusion of seasonal workers from outside the eu in these procedures. i also call for better access to information for employees about their rights and for a system of protection against abuse or exploitation. it is necessary to be able to control the employer and the system of penalties. however, they should also apply to workers who, for example, illegally extend their stay.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr moraes' report because i believe it is necessary and ethically right to improve the conditions of entry and residence of all third-country nationals who come to a member state for seasonal work. the exploitation of seasonal workers must be combated by introducing rules to regulate the flow of migration, to provide guarantees not only to the host countries but also to the workers themselves. all this in order to regulate better a phenomenon which sometimes takes on emergency features and which sees the safety of our citizens protected, along with the essential guarantees of solidarity and welcome.
in writing. - it is the first attempt to provide a comprehensive solution to the problem of seasonal workers from third countries. by ensuring that regulations are in place on accommodation standards, length of stay, labour rights and non-discrimination, it can be expected that the fundamental rights of all third-country seasonal workers will be protected in the future. the new law will allow for controlled labour migration of unskilled seasonal workers and will help to reduce the grey area. the s&d group secured the adoption of the first post-lisbon legal migration instrument.

in writing. - the situation on the insurance market for natural and man-made disasters varies widely across the eu, due in particular to the many meteorological and geographical conditions in the various member states. however, natural and man-made disasters pose financial risks wherever they occur, and the priority is to prevent and optimise the risks and exposure of eu citizens. while natural disasters are influenced by weather and geography, man-made disasters can also be the result of misbehavior, poor risk management or neglect, and a lack of preparation and information. many people choose to buy insurance, but natural and man-made disasters require different types of insurance and are covered by two different insurance markets. it is important that all insurance products available on the market provide adequate protection for eu citizens and that consumers are clearly informed about the product chosen, its price and how the insurance works in the event of a risk. i welcome the call for closer cooperation between member states and the private sector to provide citizens with relevant information on the risks they face and to exchange best practices on protecting citizens from unexpected accidents.
in writing. sometimes the responsibility for a disaster falls on a man. it can be caused by simple oversight, failure to follow procedures, or ignoring the first symptoms of tragedy. failure to take appropriate action at the right time is a sign of poor risk management. this results in inadequate preparedness of services to respond immediately in the event of a natural disaster. the resulting damage is greater than if the proper precautions had been taken and the population had been informed in advance of the impending cataclysm. it is therefore essential to develop effective communication methods to enable the rapid transmission of data on a possible disaster between the relevant services and the inhabitants of the affected area, and to place greater emphasis on scientific research to enable the rapid and accurate collection of such data. as regards insurance per se, the diversity of eu regions is such that services of this type must be geared to the area and must take account of a number of factors in contracts, such as climatic conditions, risk management methods or the effectiveness of preventive action by local services and authorities. the insurance system must therefore be flexible and 'tailored' to the needs of the region.
in writing. - the position adopted today is of great importance for competition policy. the agreement with switzerland will contribute to more effective enforcement of competition law. it is an innovative agreement, as switzerland is the eu's third largest trading partner and the second largest source of eu foreign direct investment. the two economies are closely interlinked and many anticompetitive practices affect crossborder trade. the rules and practices between the eu and switzerland are quite similar, so the implementation of this agreement should be quite easy. the main issue is the enforcement of competition law. in a world of globalised economies and global value chains, anti-competitive behaviour such as abuse of a dominant market position or cartels is a serious non-tariff barrier to trade. in this context, it is essential from the perspective of regulating foreign trade and investment to redouble efforts to promote international cooperation to combat anti-competitive practices.
in writing. - the competitiveness of the european economy is the basis for its development. cooperation agreements on competition law enforcement, such as the agreement with switzerland, are increasingly becoming the appropriate form of cooperation in an increasingly globalised world. the strategic geographical location of switzerland for the eu, the presence of a large number of eu companies in switzerland and swiss companies in the union, and the number of parallel proceedings conducted by the courts in both countries in the recent past suggest that such an agreement has become necessary. it will be important to continue to fight cartels with determination, as they harm consumer welfare, innovation and the competitiveness of both economies. the effective cooperation of the national competition authorities with the european commission will be necessary for the smooth implementation of the agreement and it will be necessary to ensure that the procedural guarantees granted to the parties in their legal systems are respected. i supported this report because i believe that these types of agreements are very innovative and will improve the competitiveness of european companies and the european economy. in addition, in certain situations, the agreement could be considered as a model for future bilateral cooperation agreements in the field of competition enforcement. however, the eu should adopt a general framework establishing a minimum common and coherent basis for any future negotiations on competition enforcement cooperation, to which the report also refers.
in writing. the arms trade treaty is designed to regulate the international trade in conventional weapons. a broad coalition in the european parliament, led by david martin, is about to give the green light to member states to sign an arms trade treaty, which aims to regulate the global market and fight illegal trade. the treaty was adopted by the un general assembly on 2 april 2013. it raises standards and standardizes procedures for arms exports and transfers, and brokering and transit. the treaty should now be implemented with ambition and progress monitored. in addition, the eu should make every effort to help develop codes of conduct for arms trading companies to promote responsible corporate behaviour.
in writing. - the resolution we recently voted on is a multilateral agreement to regulate the trade in conventional weapons. i think we need to ratify this treaty. in recent years, the dangers of uncontrolled arms trade and its destabilizing effect on armed conflicts around the world have become especially evident. it should be borne in mind, however, that the sovereignty of states is limited by the ratification of this treaty. nevertheless, i believe that the control of the trade in conventional weapons will have a positive impact on the international environment.
in writing. - in today's vote i supported the report on protection against dumped and subsidised imports from non-eu countries. the above reform package aims to modernise the existing rules in such a way as to ensure the most effective protection of union producers against dumped and subsidised imports of goods from outside the eu. the main changes relate to the tightening of the rules on the lesser duty rule in anti-dumping proceedings, the protection of the union industry by the initiation of an ex-officio investigation or the reimbursement of duties collected from importers during the expiry review. in addition, the new provisions will ensure greater predictability for traders by modifying the so-called 'shipping clause' relating to the provision of adequate advance notice to importers of the imposition of provisional duties. i believe that in the light of the changing economic situation in the world, the amendment of the proposed rules will have a fundamental impact on better protecting the interests of european producers and importers and will also help to minimise unfair trading practices.
in writing. - i believe that the union's trade defence instruments should properly reflect the interests of european producers, importers and consumers. european tdi rules are already quite liberal and take account of importers' interests at many stages. the balance between their interests and those of the european producers, whom these proceedings are designed to protect, is therefore absolutely necessary to ensure the competitiveness of our industry. we must remember that the eu is dependent on raw materials from outside the eu. any undercutting of the raw material prices on foreign markets makes those producers very competitive with the union producers. it's not their market advantage, it's a completely artificial advantage that's only been gained through government intervention. the so-called lesser duty rule is also a big problem. applying this principle puts european companies at a disadvantage compared to their competitors abroad, because in eu safeguard proceedings foreign exporters who take the market away from our producers by unfair trading practices such as dumping or subsidies can obtain a duty lower than the dumping margin, thanks to the lesser duty principle. i have supported the solutions that have been developed to address these problems and i hope that further negotiations on this issue will allow the development of effective instruments for trade protection and thus increase the competitiveness of our european businesses.
in writing. - europe, for many reasons, will never be self-sufficient, so good economic links around the world must be sought and nurtured. but we should take action to protect our businesses and consumers from unfair traders who do not respect competition rules. i therefore support the modification of the anti-dumping duty rules and the introduction of new rules to improve transparency and predictability. in doing so, care should be taken to avoid any disruption to the market, while remaining prudent. attention should be paid to unfair practices by third countries, especially in the trade of raw materials which they sell to europe at exorbitant prices. as a result, our companies, by using these materials, lose out to companies that use products purchased at original prices. the reverse mechanisms, namely the sale of subsidised products to the eu at undercutting prices, which are then uncompetitive for the eu producers, without any co-financing, should also be opposed. we must firmly oppose such practices and allow the eu institutions to do whatever they can.
in writing. - i welcome the proposed amendments to protect the european market from too cheap imports. the improvement of the functioning of the market surveillance instruments will allow the economies of the member states to be better protected against acts detrimental to the group of union producers concerned. the increase in customs duties will result in the discouragement of imports of dumped or subsidised goods from third countries into the union market, which will largely contribute to the stabilisation of polish industry and the securing of jobs for polish workers. the limitation resulting from the increase in the duty on the inflow of intermediate goods which are used to manufacture union export products will contribute to a large extent to the economic growth in the eu resulting from the stimulation of local economies. the commission has not established that the union industry is able to benefit from the measures in force. given the benefits of better import control and the opportunities it creates, i will vote in favour of adopting the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community and council regulation (ec) no 597/2009 on protection against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european community.
in writing. - the rules on compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy must be brought into line with the provisions of the lisbon treaty, which entered into force on 1 december 2009. the correct application of the co-decision procedures, delegated acts and implementing acts requires changes to the sectoral regulations. this report concerns council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system for ensuring compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. the author proposes to amend the commission proposal so that the powers conferred on the commission are reviewed after three years, when the commission presents a report on the work on the common fisheries policy (acts adopted or controls carried out during this period). it also notes certain elements of regulation (ec) no 1224/2009, such as the conditions for exempting small vessels from the obligation to hold a fishing authorisation and the conditions for awarding and transferring points for infringements. those rules should be amended so that their enforcement does not impose an additional administrative burden on fishermen.
in writing. - the largest amount of money, some 4.3 billion out of almost 6.4 billion euros, will go to sustainable fisheries between 2014 and 2020, i.e. those that take care of the recovery of fish stocks and aquaculture. the negotiators of the european parliament, the governments and the european commission have reached a preliminary agreement on the rules for spending the funds earmarked for the financing of the eu's fisheries policy in the new financial perspective. the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) will also be available to fishermen to replace engines in their boats. half-time breaks are also subsidized. the emff is to be one of the key elements of the reform of the common fisheries policy. it will help finance projects that create jobs and improve the quality of life of communities living on europe's coasts.
madam president! the adaptation of the directives to the new legal framework has created a coherent mechanism which i hope will help us to avoid all kinds of misunderstandings and unjustified differences. the improvement is expected to lead to a reduction in administrative barriers and lower costs in this segment of the economy, which will directly contribute to job growth. the inconsistent implementation of the existing rules has led to interpretation difficulties in different countries, which has created unequal market conditions. it also limited the necessary supervision of activities related to the trade in dangerous materials such as pyrotechnic articles. these and similar inaccuracies are a major obstacle to the development of the european single market. i therefore believe that the solutions proposed in these reports should be supported. at the same time, they will contribute to enhancing consumer protection by improving the safety of the products offered.
in writing. - if the explosive atmosphere contains different types of gases, vapours, mists or dust, protective measures should be applied to the greatest potential hazard. when determining the measures to prevent ignition in an explosive atmosphere, the employer should also take into account the electrostatic charges transmitted by the workers. in order to reduce such ignition, the employer shall ensure that persons working are provided with appropriate clothing which will not contribute to the generation of electrostatic discharges. the explosion protection documentation shall also specify which installations, devices, protective systems and connecting elements, in particular cables, wires, pipes, can be safely used in an explosive atmosphere. this also applies to devices and components which are not considered to be protective devices or systems if their incorporation into the installation is liable to cause a risk of ignition. the employer shall be responsible for taking measures to prevent the wrong connection of the coupling elements. the employer must also take the necessary measures to ensure that workplaces, equipment and connecting elements accessible to workers are designed, constructed, assembled and installed, and maintained and operate in such a way as to minimise the risk of explosion.
in writing. - the objective of harmonising the laws of the member states relating to the making available on the market and the control of explosives for civil use is first and foremost to ensure the highest level of protection and safety for eu citizens. all explosives intended for civil use should meet the essential safety requirements before being made available on the market. i supported the new legal framework as it introduces simplified product regulations and allows for more consistent application of technical standards, which will help improve the functioning of the single market by ensuring equal treatment of non-compliant products and equal assessment of notified bodies within the eu market. this will increase confidence of both producers and consumers by clarifying the obligations of economic operators and equip member states' authorities with more effective tools for carrying out controls and market surveillance, leading to a reduction in the number of non-compliant and dangerous products.
in writing. - trading explosives requires special security. the obligation to label a new (unmarked) material is imposed on an undertaking carrying out the business of trading in explosives for civil use when it places the material on the market. what does that mean? it is necessary to provide the name of the manufacturer, the alphanumeric code and the electronically readable marking. this is just one of several provisions of the law on the conduct of this type of business that is now coming into force. the two regulations relating to the labelling of materials enter into force at the same time. they shall establish a register of unique indications, the rules for which shall depend on the activity which the operator wishes to pursue. this includes manufacturing and trading or activities carried out by scientific units. the data collected in the register shall be kept for 10 years from the date of manufacture of the material intended for civil use or until the time of its use or destruction. the trader shall be obliged to provide the data entered in the register at the request of the competent authorities and services. the new rules also define the production site. this is the organized part of the enterprise where explosives for civilian use are manufactured.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the harmonisation of the provisions of the member states relating to the making available on the market of non-automatic weighing instruments. the report aims to amend the existing directive 2009/23/ec, which is part of the package of nine eu goods directives adopted by the commission in 2008 as part of the implementation of the new legal framework (nlf). strengthening the procedures for making non-automatic weighing instruments available on the market will have a significant impact on the safety of those products sold in the union, will contribute to their better functioning in the single market and will thus benefit both manufacturers, importers and distributors. in addition, the tightening of legislation will protect the eu market from the influx of goods that do not comply with european standards. i believe that another important benefit of the harmonisation of the rules on non-automatic weighing instruments is the reduction of the administrative burden and thus the reduction of the costs incurred. i am of the opinion that, in order to ensure adequate safety in the sale and distribution of the products in question, it is also necessary to strengthen market surveillance by the member states. this will help to avoid the placing on the market of dangerous products that do not comply with eu standards and will increase the level of consumer protection.
in writing. - non-automatic weighing instruments are measuring instruments used to determine the weight of a body by applying gravity to the body, requiring the intervention of an operator during weighing (e.g. when a load is placed on a scale). the scale may also be used to determine other parameters or properties related to mass, size, quantity or properties.
in writing. - the need to meet emc requirements does not mean that the product must be tested by a certified laboratory, as the manufacturer (or importer) assumes responsibility for compliance with the standards by issuing an appropriate declaration of conformity. products for which a declaration of conformity has been drawn up shall be presumed to comply with the requirements of union law and to be honest. however, the president of the office for electronic communications is empowered to verify the declaration and to verify that the equipment actually complies with the requirements of the directive. where such non-compliance is found, the manufacturer may be fined, ordered to withdraw the device from the market or prohibited from reselling it. the assessment of the conformity of the equipment with the emc directive is possible in principle only after the relevant tests have been carried out.
in writing. - the essential characteristics, knowledge of and application of which will ensure that electrical equipment is used safely and for its intended purpose, should be visible on the electrical equipment and, if not, should be indicated in the accompanying documentation. for the purposes of directive 2006/95/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2006 on the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to electrical equipment designed for use within certain voltage limits (oj l 374, 27.12.2006, p. 10, the so-called low voltage directive), 'electrical equipment' means any equipment intended for use at voltages between 50 v and 1 000 v ac and between 75 v and 1 500 v dc, with the exception of equipment and phenomena listed in annex ii.
in writing. - electric elevators, commonly known as elevators, are commonly used devices. every day, millions of people and goods are moved around the world by crane in the traffic lanes of residential, office, commercial, and industrial buildings. lifts are also widely used in industry, in factories and in mine shafts. a crane is a lifting device that is part of a crane, i.e. a means of transport with a limited range and intermittent, vertical or horizontal movement. lifts are used to move cargo or people in cabins or on platforms. they are usually located in closed or partially open windows of brick, concrete or glass construction. the vertical inclination of the aperture shall not exceed 15°.
in writing. - directive 2009/105/ec of 16 september 2009 relating to simple pressure vessels, referred to as the spvd directive for short, concerns simple pressure vessels produced in series. a simple pressure vessel is any welded vessel subject to an internal overpressure of more than 0,5 bar, designed for the storage of air or nitrogen and not intended for heating by flame.
in writing. - magnetoelectric measuring instruments, measuring instruments of constant electric current (or other physical quantities converted into electric current) in which the measurement is made by the interaction of the magnetic field of a permanent magnet (magnes) with the field produced by the measured current flowing in a moving coil connected to a guide. the interaction of the fields creates a torque compensated by the torque of the reciprocating forces generated by the elastic fixing of the coil, the position of the balance of the torques of the forces being proportional to the current flowing in the coil. magnetoelectric measuring instruments are used as amperometers, voltmeters and ohmometers.
in writing. - most air passengers have experienced, at least once, cases of flight overbooking, long delays, flight cancellations, or mishandled luggage. out of those entitled to compensation, only 2% of passengers have actually obtained it. as the eu aviation sector continues to grow, so does the need to better protect the rights of air passengers. with that aim, the bach report calls for the revision of the current eu regulation on passenger's rights. the report asks that information about rights be more available to air passengers and consumers, as well as assistance mechanisms to handle passengers' complaints. furthermore, the text touches upon the issue of compensation by setting regulations which will make it harder for airlines to avoid paying. equally important, the report asks airlines to end their "no show" policy, this way passengers' will be able to board return flight even-though they have been absent for the outward journey. while managing to strike a reasonable balance between the airlines and the passenger rights, the report gives consumers better understanding of their rights and effective tools to safeguard them. this is an important step for increasing the standards of services offered to air passengers, therefore i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - with the number of air passengers in the european union increasing year by year, there is a need for comprehensive and coherent rules on compensation and assistance in the event of denied boarding or cancellation or long delay of flights. unfortunately, european consumer passengers still complain about the unsatisfactory level of protection in the event of delays, cancellations or other disruptive changes to flights. provisions are necessary to ensure that passengers are informed in a clear and comprehensible manner and as soon as possible of any disruption to their journey, its causes and their rights in the event of such disruption. it is also necessary to ensure that passengers' rights to compensation are enforced more effectively and more quickly, while ensuring a fair balance between the interests of passengers and air carriers.
in writing. - european society is becoming more mobile. working in another country, studying or going abroad for weekends makes us use air transport more often. this is also due to the increasingly better prices offered by carriers. unfortunately, the rights of passengers are often violated. airlines exploit loopholes in the law in cases of delays, lost baggage, flight cancellations or so-called overbooking. even before the journey begins, passengers' rights are not respected by presenting unclear ticket prices, which do not include surcharges and do not take into account taxes. after all, airline passengers are consumers just as you are when you buy food or other goods or services. the report therefore implements provisions designed to facilitate travel through a clear and transparent legislative framework, with regard to the rights and obligations of customers and carriers. clear rules will avoid misunderstandings for both parties. an important aspect of the report is the argument that a guarantee fund should be created to provide security for passengers in the event of the insolvency of the carrier.
in writing. - passenger rights are crucial for our citizens. being delayed or even trapped at an airport due to the bankruptcy of an airline is only the worst scenario what can happen. i believe that in the report i supported with my vote in favour, the european parliament will deliver solutions to our citizens, especially when it comes to reasonable compensation in case of delays, bankruptcy insurance for airlines and a coherent onboard luggage rule. i congratulate the rapporteur for his excellent work.
in writing. - according to the montreal convention, a passenger may claim compensation up to 1131 sdrs (pln 5670,16 at the average nbp exchange rate of 13.11.2012). the current sdr exchange rate is available on the official website of the national bank of poland: www.nbp.pl. it should be noted that the amount of 1131 sdrs is not a lump sum for the injured passenger but only the upper limit of the carrier's liability in the event of delay, loss or damage to luggage. obtaining compensation depends on several important factors and it is the consumer who is obliged to prove the damage suffered.
in writing. - the basic condition for declaring bankruptcy is the insolvency of the debtor, i.e. generally the state in which he fails to meet his due obligations or when they exceed the value of his assets. in order to be able to declare bankruptcy, the delay in the execution of these obligations should be longer than 3 months, unless the non-execution of the obligations is of a permanent nature and a continuation of such a state could cause prejudice to the creditors. the bankruptcy notice may be requested by any of them. in the case of a public, partnership, limited partnership or limited-liability company, any of the partners, partners or shareholders (including liquidators if it is in liquidation) may also do so, and in the case of legal persons and other organisational units, anyone who has the right to represent them (in the case of a bank, only the banking supervision commission has the right to make such a request). this right becomes an obligation if the entrepreneur himself ceases to pay his debts. he is then obliged to apply to the court for a declaration of bankruptcy no later than two weeks after the event. if he fails to do so, he may be liable for damage caused by his inaction.
in writing. - unfortunately, in today's united europe, corporate bankruptcies have become a common occurrence, to which this chamber full of unclear regulations adds its brick. it is sufficient to mention that during this session more than 4300 small and medium-sized enterprises in europe went bankrupt. the basic condition for declaring bankruptcy is the insolvency of the debtor, i.e. generally the state in which the debtor fails to meet its due obligations or when they exceed the value of its assets. in order to be able to declare bankruptcy, the delay in the execution of these obligations should be longer than 3 months, unless the non-execution of the obligations is of a permanent nature and a continuation of such a state could cause prejudice to the creditors. in respect of a public, partnership, limited partnership or limited partnership, any of the partners, partners or shareholders may also do so. this right becomes an obligation if the entrepreneur himself ceases to pay his debts. he is then obliged to file a bankruptcy petition with the court within two weeks at the latest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr lehne on the reform of the insolvency law in the european union because i believe that the times of crisis have shown us where we need to improve the legislation in this area. the free market enables companies to grow, establish branches and subsidiaries throughout the union. however, at the time of the bankruptcy declaration, when the creditors are waiting for their money, it turns out that the cross-border procedure is very complicated and takes an infinite amount of time, leaving the victims without compensation for many months. the changes proposed in the report are designed to speed up cross-border proceedings and to coordinate insolvency proceedings within a group of companies. i hope that the council, following the european parliament's lead, will also work vigorously on this regulation, because the union is in dire need of effective rules on crossborder insolvency proceedings.

in writing. - i voted in favour of amending the existing regulations (ec) no 261/2004 and (ec) no 2027/97 laying down the rules on aid and compensation to passengers in the event of denied boarding, cancellation or long delay of flights. the increase in the number of flights and therefore in the number of passengers using airlines has led to a decline in the quality of services provided by air carriers and to frequent non-compliance with the rights of their passengers. the purpose of this regulation is therefore to strengthen the rules in respect of airline passengers. the proposed amendments classify their rights to assistance and compensation in the event of long delays in flight schedules in a more transparent manner. other regulations relate to the rights of passengers in the event of connecting flights, denied boarding, exceptional circumstances or emergency plans. i am convinced that the adoption of this report in today's vote will ensure that european union passengers can exercise their rights more efficiently and transparently and will also contribute to improving the level of service provided by air carriers.
in writing. - the need to harmonise passenger protection legislation through common regulations is of the utmost importance. the very frequent occurrence of flight delays or cancellations is a source of serious problems for passengers, both professional and financial. passengers who are denied boarding, as well as those whose flights are delayed or cancelled altogether, should be protected by the right to assistance in the purchase of new tickets and other facilities to increase the comfort of waiting for the next or delayed flight. an essential element of such protection is the right to fair compensation based on the failure or improper performance of an obligation by the carrier or the airport administration.
in writing. - almost all of us have been in a situation where a flight is delayed. in such situations, several airlines, especially the so-called low-cost airlines, do not provide passengers with any compensation for delayed flights. the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market. i therefore supported the proposal that airlines should compensate passengers whose flights are delayed or cancelled. the new rules reduce the time of flight delays, after which passengers are entitled to receive meals from the airline, to make a telephone call and, if necessary, to be accommodated. the new rules also provide that passengers are entitled to a refund of the price of a flight if it is cancelled or delayed for more than three hours, and also if they require a free flight to the required destination. the improvements also include the possibility for passengers to bring a coat, a hand baggage bag and a shopping bag with their airport purchases free of charge. similarly, a person may not be able to use a purchased airline ticket. in this case, most airlines do not provide a refund. i therefore supported the provision that a passenger is entitled to a refund of airport taxes even if he cancels his flight. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on 28 june 2010 and that the agreement was signed on 27 june 2010. failure to comply with the deadline would mean that the air carrier agrees to meet the customer's demands. thank you.

mr. chairman, please! energy and climate policy is one of the key activities both in the economic sphere and for the energy security of the community. unfortunately, current strategies tend to ignore the need to treat the most important areas equally, such as diversification, security of supply and the competitiveness of european businesses. i believe that the greenhouse gas reduction ceilings already in place are too high, are being implemented at the expense of other projects and are imposing an undue burden on businesses. so i agree with the argument that there is no justification for setting specific, precise values at such an early stage. flexibility in how countries achieve their reduction targets seems desirable. the results of international negotiations on climate packages and agreements on this matter should also be awaited.
in writing. - global warming is one of the biggest challenges facing the developed world today. according to un data, global co2 emissions increased by more than 50% between 1990 and 2010. the report adopted today sets out the eu's long-term policy for the new 2030 framework for climate and energy policy, which will replace the existing 2020 framework. the resolution calls on the member states to reduce co2 emissions by at least 40%, to obtain 30% of energy from renewable sources and to achieve 40% energy efficiency. i support strengthening climate policy and investing in renewable energy, but i believe that the dual goal of reducing emissions after 2020 is unrealistic and could reduce the competitiveness of european industry. the proposed targets do not take into account the specificities of the member states. and it is european governments that should set their own national targets for renewable energy and energy efficiency. i also agree with the comments that a specific co2 emission reduction ceiling should only be set after the conference of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change in paris in 2015, where the most responsible emitters will set their binding targets.
in writing. - i voted 'no' because the report did not adequately address the theses in my amendments, which were: better use of peak capacity in view of the different longitude of the union and the difference in astronomical time; construction of new south-bound transmission networks from wind farms installed in the north of the eu, i.e. over the north sea or the baltic, as well as those installed directly on those waters; greater attention to undervalued and under-researched energy sources; a shift away from the rhetorical doctrine of total decarbonisation of the economy to a reduction in gross emissions per unit of gdp; the need to take account of the energy policy objectives of the eu's primary energy source, i.e. the ets, and the need to increase the eu's carbon dioxide emissions by 3%, in line with the current policy; a shift away from the rhetorical doctrine of a total decarbonisation of the economy to a reduction in the energy efficiency of the eu's primary energy source, i.e. the eu's primary energy policy, and the need to increase its carbon dioxide emissions by 3%, based on the current policy; a shift away from the political need to a political and technological policy of absorption of carbon dioxide. i also pointed out that it is currently unrealistic to push for a single eu-wide energy paradigm based solely on renewable energy sources, because a methodological error is being made due to the fact that the distribution of these sources is uneven.
in writing. - i voted against this report. i think that at this stage it was not necessary to have it, and certainly not to have it in such a hurry. the debate on the strategic climate policy post-2020 should be left to the next parliamentary term, and it should be a substantive debate, taking into account environmental and climate objectives, but also the impact of their introduction on the competitiveness of the european economy and energy prices. today, instead of a substantive debate, ideological manifestos have been presented. we must not forget that, paradoxically, europe's overly strict climate standards may contribute to the global increase in greenhouse gas emissions. i fear that the european socialists and the greens, by setting out ambitious climate targets, will lead to a repeat of the lisbon strategy or the collapse of the european economy. and they're not going to save the climate, because the industry that leaves europe will be emitting even more greenhouse gases outside the eu. a separate comment is made on the scandalous treatment of the rapporteur by the vice-president of the ep who was in charge of the vote and the fact that he was not allowed to speak before the final vote.
in writing. - we want to fight climate change. we want to develop the renewable energy sector. we want to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. these are all noble goals, and we're committed to protecting the environment and ensuring access to clean energy for future generations. i'll take that. but when we implement solutions such as emissions trading, the use of a specific level of biofuels in transport or 'greening' agriculture, we cannot be guided by purely utopian motives. we need to look at the state of the economy, the energy sector, transport and agriculture here and now, look at the differences between the different regions of europe, and think about how to protect the earth's ecosystems without causing economic disaster in some countries. if a country's energy is based on coal, we cannot expect that country to radically transform its energy sector in a few years without disastrous consequences for the economy. we cannot ask the government of a country like that to take hundreds of thousands of jobs away from climate targets, to have farmers modernize their farms and change their business profile in an instant, and to have entrepreneurs abandon investments that were started just a few years ago and make new ones to change technology in a flash. these are not processes that can happen at the touch of a magic wand. we need transitional periods, aid schemes, restructuring support. let us not make hasty decisions that could seriously damage europe's economy.
in writing. - i decided, along with the majority of polish mps, to vote against the report because i thought it went too far. i believe that it will have a negative impact on the negotiating position of the polish government at the next climate summits and will contribute to the further elimination of coal as an energy source, which in turn will hit the polish economy. the drastic reduction of co2 emissions that the report proposes and the total elimination of coal from the energy sector after 2050 are contrary to poland's interests. this will further depend on russian gas supplies for the energy sector and drive up the price of co2 trading. we cannot allow future generations of poles to pay for the reckless and top-down climate policy goals of europe.

in writing. - this own-initiative report is intended to guide the commission's further action on future binding 2030 climate and energy policy targets. but the question is: in the absence of an analysis of the implementation of the current political commitments, should the unrealistic ambitions imposed by the green group in the face of worsening competitiveness, industrial relocation and rising unemployment be so strongly supported by us socialists? i disagree with some of the arguments made by our colleagues in the group of the european people's party who are fighting hard to make this central element of the green group's programme a central element of the s&d group's programme. why would you do that? because it will have a negative impact on the social situation in our countries in the future. the current regulations in the so-called climate and energy package have already caused a lot of damage.
in writing. - a swift completion of the banking union is essential to ensure financial stability and economic growth in the euro area and the internal market as a whole. a banking union will overcome the current fragmentation of financial markets in europe and reduce the uncertainty that was one of the causes of the euro area crisis. it will also prevent taxpayers from paying for bank bailouts in the future. to this end, it is proposed to set up a rescue fund to which the banks themselves will contribute. with the agreement on pillar i of the banking union, i.e. a single, common banking supervisory framework, we are entering the crucial phase of work on pillar ii, i.e. a common framework for the restructuring and orderly winding-up of banks. the commission's proposed directive on this subject, once adopted by the european parliament and the council, will set out rules for the restructuring of banks in the eu that are experiencing serious financial difficulties and for maintaining their functions that are essential for the real economy, as well as rules for the sharing of losses and costs between shareholders, creditors and unsecured depositors of these banks. it is also necessary to speed up work on the last pillar of the banking union, namely the common deposit guarantee scheme.
in writing. - the legislative proposal from the european commission establishing a single resolution mechanism for all credit institutions established in the euro area and other member states participating in the single supervisory mechanism, including a single resolution fund fund fund funded by all financial institutions covered by it on an ex-ante basis and taking into account risk, is a necessary step towards the creation of a genuine banking union. this is an ambitious and balanced proposal, necessary to create a strong framework for dealing with future banking crises in the euro area (and participating member states). the proposal sets out three main objectives: to avoid costs for taxpayers, to protect deposits and to limit external damage in the event of an uncontrolled bankruptcy, especially for the real economy.

madam president! the legislation that calls for a reduction in the carbon emissions of new passenger cars to 95 grams of carbon dioxide per kilometer by 2020, coupled with changes in production and so-called super-units, is the beginning of a so-called revolution. this is going to be a revolution for the 21st century, and it's going to show us what we can do in the automotive industry. and the important thing is that this is driven, in a sense, by the climate itself, but it's also driven by new activities, like the fuel prices that are in place right now. and we also have to realize that all of these changes will also trigger the possibility of new technologies in the research units. these units were also waiting for a push to start working on new electric motors, for example. they also provide incentives for the manufacturers themselves to innovate. we just have to make sure that we don't throw the baby out with the bathtub and introduce laws and regulations that will eventually block this industry, and the rest should go in the right direction.
in writing. co2 emissions are a measure of fuel consumption and vehicle economy. the problem is not motorization, but the emission of sulphur, nitrogen, dust and co and noise. progress is about efficiency. in the derived calculation, this is the co2 emissions from combustion, car manufacturing and dismantling. japan leads the world in automobile manufacturing. the us producers, due to their lower unit costs of production, are more profitable than europe, which is losing its industrial competitiveness globally. the innovation potential of the automotive sector is very high and concerns engines, bodywork, fuels and tyres. there are many patents on innovation in the cupboards of companies that block development instead of initiating it. there are no easy objectives - europe and the world are waiting for a revolutionary breakthrough in this field - the commission's proposal must be supported. supercredit is a good incentive for companies looking for energy-efficient technologies. when analysing co2 emission figures, other co2 emission figures, such as per passenger or engine power to vehicle standard work, should be considered. the lack of competitiveness of the european automotive industry results in the relocation of automotive production to third countries not burdened by the commitments under the climate and energy package. the european car market is different from that of the usa and other non-eu countries. perhaps the solution for the eu, based on pro-environmental law, would be to tighten up the admission criteria in the member states.
madam president! the community trade mark system, which had been in place for 15 years, required modernisation of the rules and alignment of its terminology with the treaty of lisbon. the improvement of the system together with the internal market harmonisation office responsible for registration will have a significant impact on innovation and economic growth in the union through better access for businesses and simplification of trademark application procedures. online sales in the union have increased significantly in recent years: 61% of users bought products online, an increase of 11% compared to 2008. the main objective of the existing community system and of economic property rights at national level is to prevent fraud as regards the origin and quality of products. the current changes will make it much more difficult to introduce counterfeit goods into the union (especially in online sales). however, i believe that the legal instruments enabling the trade mark proprietor to take action to prevent the import of counterfeit goods or to initiate legal proceedings against persons committing misuse should be clarified, together with the weakening of the authorities responsible for monitoring websites selling such items. the elimination of divergences in the rules of the current legal framework and the coexistence of the union system with national systems are the basis for a well-functioning internal market.
on behalf of the ecr group. - madam president! - i have to go. crime can't pay. that's the basic meaning of punishing criminals. the state judiciary cannot be limited to the criminal punishment of deprivation of liberty or restriction of the freedom of the convicted person, but should do everything to deprive the offender of any benefits derived from the crime. everything he has obtained through crime, what he has stolen, what he has robbed or, for example, bought with the benefits obtained through corruption, should be effectively taken away from him. if the crime has caused harm to someone, the benefits should be used to repair that harm, and if the harm is in the interest of the state, the confiscated property should become the property of the state. if the criminal loses all the benefits of his crime, if he repairs the damage, only then does justice become full. only then does punishing criminals prevent future crimes. this is the purpose of the directive we are discussing today. it is a good directive, allowing for more effective prosecution and punishment of criminals, for a fairer punishment. that's why i'm supporting her.
the confiscation of proceeds of crime laws in many eu countries are ineffective. criminal suspects, operating in organised groups, transfer their assets to third parties and to other countries. this is facilitated by the lengthy legal proceedings and the practice of confiscation only after a conviction. then there's often nothing left to confiscate. this pathology needs to be changed. in the most serious cases, the choice is between direct confiscation, confiscation of the equivalent of the property or confiscation of the property transferred to a third party. it would also be necessary for all eu countries to mutually recognise the possibility of confiscating and freezing the proceeds of crime. while i agree with these harsh measures, i would point out that they should be applied provided that decisions are taken by the judicial authorities, with due regard for the rights of the defence. we must act decisively and quickly, but these cannot be administrative decisions, but always decisions of the judicial authorities.

in writing. the european semester, or european evaluation period for economic policy coordination, was established by one of the six-pack regulations in november 2011. it is the basic framework for enhanced economic governance in the eu. it is designed to combine the actions provided for in the europe 2020 strategy and the so-called fiscal compact. we are now in the fourth cycle of the european semester. importantly, there are already some signs of improvement in the european economy this year. some euro area countries in crisis and following difficult reforms are slowly coming to terms their trade imbalances are narrowing and competitiveness is increasing. this in turn translates into a slow return of confidence in financial markets and a fall in the cost of debt financing. the most urgent task facing the eu, and the euro area in particular, is to complete as soon as possible the construction of a banking union based on three pillars: a common single system of financial supervision, a common system for the orderly resolution of banks and a common deposit guarantee scheme. we are nearing the end of the second pillar of the banking union, which should be in place before the european elections. so there's a chance that we could have the whole structure completed in the next few years. the banking union should help to protect the eu from similar crises in the future.

in writing. - in today's vote, i voted in favor of the community trade mark. it focuses on the review of the eu's trademark registration system, which has been in place for more than 15 years. the current system needs to be modernised in several respects, according to studies carried out by the european commission. first of all, the rapporteur proposes to modernise and update the rules, specifying the scope of trademark rights, which will eliminate the existing ambiguities. the next step is to harmonise trademark registration procedures in all member states, taking into account the cooperation between the eu agency office for harmonization in the internal market and national offices, which is necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. another very important point is to streamline the legal means to enable trademark owners to take action to block the import of counterfeit goods into the eu. i believe that the adoption of the proposed changes to the community trade mark will reduce costs and simplify the registration process, which will improve the conditions for european businesses to operate. moreover, modernising the existing rules will help to improve innovation in europe and thus stimulate economic growth.
in writing. - a trade mark is important for the competitiveness of an enterprise because it allows the goods or services offered by a given enterprise to be distinguished from those offered by other enterprises and thus improves the position of the enterprises. i supported the report because the changes are improving the community trade mark system, which has already proved to be a great success. the new challenges of orphan works and intellectual property infringement require a new approach to these issues. the office for harmonization in the internal market is the competent body to address these challenges and i therefore consider it appropriate to increase its competence in this area. the brand should be seen as a driving force for innovation. it not only helps companies to acquire new customers, but also to build long-term trust between these customers and their company. the small business card provides for the enhancement of the accessibility of the community trade mark system to smes. the duration of the procedure is particularly challenging, as are the costs, which can be a major barrier for small businesses. of course, national trademark systems are still necessary for those companies that do not seek eu-wide protection for their trademarks. the report will stimulate innovation and growth by making trade mark registration systems more accessible to businesses and more efficient across the eu, thereby ensuring complementarity between the eu and national trade mark registration systems.
in writing. - a community trade mark may be obtained by registration at the office for harmonization in the internal market in alicante, spain. the authority shall be an agency of the union. investments in e-business tools allow him to connect with businesses around the world via the internet. a community trade mark may consist of any sign capable of being represented graphically, in particular of words (including names), drawings, letters, figures, the shape of goods or their packaging, provided that such signs enable the goods or services of one undertaking to be distinguished from those of other undertakings.

in writing. - trade mark law in the eu has been harmonised. the new rules in this area strengthen the harmonising aspects of the law and procedures applied by national trade mark offices. at present, a community trade mark coexists with national trade marks. it is important to maintain this dual system, because for those companies that do not seek to have their trademarks protected throughout the eu, it is the mark protected in the territory of a particular member state that has the real added value. some companies need protection for their trademark in only one country, while others are interested in protection throughout the european union. the needs of companies are different. the trade mark system should be sufficiently simple and flexible to give users of the system access to protection appropriate to their needs. it may still happen that a company does not seek protection throughout the eu, but also that it does not seek protection in just one country, but for example in several. in such situations, clear and simple procedures for obtaining protection in each country are particularly important in order to make national trademark systems more attractive to users. and these regulations will make it easier. the review of existing legislation protects and strengthens this two-tiered trademark system in europe.
in writing. - on 27 march 2013, the european commission presented a package of initiatives to streamline and improve trademark registration systems and to ensure their protection is more effective and reliable. it is now more than 20 years since the first directive aimed at harmonising trade mark law and more than 15 since the creation of the community trade mark. the system worked, but now it needs improvement. the earlier amendments to those provisions, which resulted in the directive and regulation currently in force, were of an orderly nature. now, after two decades, the time has come for the next step, which is to mainly harmonise the registration systems of the member states. the proposed amendments reflect experience gained and were considered on the basis of a report by the max planck institute on the functioning of the trade mark systems of the member states and the community system.
in writing. - new trademarks appear on the market almost daily, becoming a valuable asset for a company and an essential element in the promotion of the goods or services produced. however, the system is primarily aimed at consumers, who can make an informed choice by identifying the origin of the product. harmonising national systems and creating a common eu trademark at the same time was one of the first successful eu projects in the field of intellectual property law. although both the directive and the regulation have stood the test of time and their foundations are still valid, a reform is necessary to bring the law into line with current realities. the proposed amendments aim in particular to facilitate access to protection by reducing costs, simplifying procedures, increasing legal certainty and taking into account the extensive case law of the european court of justice. the coordination between national offices and ohim is also to be improved. i believe that mechanisms for quick and affordable legal protection will be a key tool for legitimate traders to effectively combat counterfeiting and to reap the benefits they deserve from the sale of genuine products. the modern system will also provide an incentive to continue to improve the offer and to build consumer confidence in european brands. i therefore fully support parliament's position today and look forward to rapid progress in the council.

in writing. - the first directive (on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of engaging in a highly skilled occupation) is implemented by the inclusion of a new chapter 4a in the aliens act. it contains provisions specifying the conditions for granting a residence permit for a specified period in poland with the intention of performing highly qualified work. the authorisation will be granted under a single administrative procedure. the deadline for the case is 90 days. the voivodeship will be obliged to determine, among other things, whether the foreigner has the appropriate qualifications, meets the salary threshold criterion and whether the employer can take advantage of job offers on the local labour market. the findings will be communicated to the voivodeship by the mayor based on an analysis of the register of unemployed and jobseekers or a negative result of the recruitment organised for the employer. when issuing a decision on granting a residence permit for a specified period in order to take up employment in poland in a profession requiring high qualifications, the governor shall examine the amount of remuneration set out in the employment contract.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation establishing the fund for european aid to the most deprived because i believe it is well placed to achieve the europe 2020 poverty reduction target of at least 20 million people. i support the establishment of a programme which introduces the possibility of allocating part of the funds to material aid in the form of non-food products and to accompanying measures aimed at the social reintegration of aid beneficiaries. while the european social fund remains the main eu instrument to increase the chances of social inclusion, especially through employment, we must bear in mind that those in need, such as the homeless or the undernourished, are often excluded from it because of their exclusion. the european fund for the most deprived is therefore an important complement to the esf. however, we must not forget that it is not a comprehensive policy strategy to reduce and eradicate poverty - it requires urgent work by the european commission and the member states. i am of the opinion that care should be taken to simplify the system of implementation and clearance of the aid granted as much as possible in order to avoid imposing excessive financial and bureaucratic burdens on the implementing entities. i believe that the system proposed in the regulation is too elaborate both in terms of the allocation of funds and the scope and type of support, and i have therefore tabled the appropriate amendments calling on the commission to simplify it.
in writing. - the battle this parliament has fought over the funds for food aid to the poor of the union has achieved a very good result. the overall ceiling of 3.5 billion over 7 years, which remains unchanged from the previous programming, despite a sharply reduced weekly budget, will ensure food aid and basic necessities for european citizens in difficulty. it is clear that the allocation of these funds is not sufficient to deal with the economic crisis, which is reflected in the growing number of people in need. more needs to be done in the coming years to protect these sections of the population, but today's result is a concrete sign of what europe can do to support its citizens, and in this case the most vulnerable sections.
in writing. - the european fund for the most deprived is a symbol of european solidarity with those most affected by the economic crisis. although the fund's budget has been increased, it is still far from sufficient. in 2010, almost a quarter of europeans (120 million people) were at risk of poverty and social exclusion. the fund for european aid to the most deprived is an instrument to alleviate the most acute forms of poverty, namely food and material deprivation, experienced by citizens in all member states. the budget of the fund is reserved for assistance to the most deprived and should not be used for activities of other cohesion funds. the european fund for the most deprived is only a complement to national policies; the responsibility for combating and eradicating poverty should lie with the member states. i have nevertheless supported mr costello's report, which i regard as good and balanced.
in writing. - the report we adopted today has been circulating in the corridors of european administration for too long. it would not be surprising if we were dealing with a complex regulation harmonising another sector of the common market and leading to deeper european integration. but we are dealing with an instrument that is supposed to function in parallel with the single market mechanisms: an instrument of direct support for those who have no chance of fully benefiting from the european economy. the economic crisis, which began six years ago, has brought an incredible impoverishment to hundreds of thousands, if not millions, of europeans, demonstrating the shortcomings of the neoliberal economic doctrine. but let us be clear: the fund for european aid to the most deprived is no panacea for economic crisis, poverty or social exclusion. solving the problems facing europe requires a deep restructuring of the single market and, above all, closer integration. it's going to take a long time. there is no doubt that the poorest europeans are looking to us for solidarity and help right now. without further ado, i call on the european commission and the governments of the member states to mobilise the fund as soon as possible and to distribute its resources fairly among those most in need.
in writing. - after more than a year of negotiations with the eu council, we have today adopted the european fund for aid to the most deprived (fead), which will replace the current food distribution programme from the common agricultural policy stocks and funds. as twice rapporteur for the european parliament on the food distribution programme, i am pleased that despite the resistance of the member states, the current level of aid, i.e. eur 3.5 billion for 7 years, is maintained, which amounts to eur 500 million per year. it is worth recalling that the european commission put forward a figure of eur 2.5 billion in its initial proposal. in 2011, thanks also to my efforts as rapporteur and the polish presidency of the council at the time, we managed to extend the previous food aid programme until the end of 2013, even though some eu countries wanted to end it by then. the continuation of the programme in its new form until at least 2020 is therefore all the more valuable. the adoption of the european fund for the most deprived is particularly important given that, as a result of the crisis, over 120 million people in the eu are already at risk of poverty or social exclusion. however, there is no doubt that the assistance offered by the union is still a proverbial drop in the ocean of needs.
in writing. - i have lent my support to the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the fund for european aid to the most deprived (com(2012)0617 – c7-0358/2012 – 2012/0295(cod)). this report outlines the disparity that has impacted many eu citizens since the economic crisis and takes full account of the necessity for further action to assist those in need. as the report states ‘the proposed eur[nbsp ]2.5 billion fund for the 2014-20 period, would establish a new, broader instrument, partly building upon the experience of the mdp by supporting national schemes that address food deprivation, whilst devoting part of its resources for material assistance in the form of non-food goods for homeless people and/or children, and for accompanying measures aimed at social reintegration of assisted personsʼ. thus, the strategy is not only to provide food and shelter for the most deprived but also to provide training and assistance in the re-entry to working society which will slowly provide the eu with the citizens needed to continue our economic recovery.
in writing. - the european commission has proposed a fund to provide aid to the most deprived people in the eu. the fund would support member states' programmes that provide food for the most deprived and clothing and other basic items for the homeless and for children in need. the proposal will now be submitted to the european parliament and the council of ministers of the european union for approval. the commission provides for a budget of eur 2,5 billion for this fund for the years 2014-2020 as part of its proposal for the multiannual financial framework of june 2011. member states would be responsible for 15% of the costs of their national programmes, with the remaining 85% of the costs being financed by the fund. at european level, we need to introduce new solidarity mechanisms and to mobilise the appropriate resources to provide assistance to the needy and the poor, who in many cases live in a truly alarming social situation. that is the objective of the european fund for aid to the most deprived approved today.

in writing. - it is an active substance or a preparation containing at least one active substance in the form in which it is supplied to the user, intended to destroy, deter, render harmless, prevent the action of, or control in any other way harmful organisms by chemical or biological action. by law, only biocidal products for which a marketing authorisation (or provisional authorisation) has been granted or which have been entered in the register of biocidal products posing a low risk may be on the market in the pr. due to their intended use, biocidal products have been divided into 4 categories and groups according to the specific intended use within each category. in order to be legally placed on the market in poland, a biocidal product must be submitted for a licence, provisional licence or registration. such an application shall be submitted by the applicant, either alone or with the assistance of a representative, to the president of the office for the registration of medicinal products, medical devices and biocidal products. the complete registration dossier should contain the data relating to the applicant, the product data, the content of the instructions for use and the product characteristics sheet. in addition, the existence of the active substance in circulation in poland before the entry into force of the biocidal products act should be documented.
in writing. - violence against women affects one in every five european women, one in every three women world-wide. it is the root cause of gender inequality and an obstacle to women’s full participation in social, political and economic life. in addition to the toll on human life and dignity, studies estimate that violence against women costs our society approximately eur 228 billion each year. regardless of these facts and figures, the eu is currently lacking both a comprehensive strategy to combat violence against women, and a legislative framework to support member states in the field of prevention. changing this reality, the current legislative report asks to establish a common eu regulation on combating violence against women that takes into consideration prevention and combat measures. more specifically, the report asks for consistent and systematic data collection at the eu level; it urges member state to sign and ratify the istanbul convention on violence against women; and it requests that financial support for equality mechanisms be established within the eu’s budget. these proposals are necessary for ensuring better protection for women and girls against all forms of violence, and, for promoting women’s rights and gender equality. therefore i voted in support this report.
