vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i would like to sincerely thank the six rapporteurs and the committee on transport and tourism for their extensive and intensive work on the fourth railway package. a year ago, the commission put forward the six legislative proposals forming the fourth railway package. the aim is to complete the internal market for rail services and create a true single european rail area. this is the dream, this is the aim and this is the purpose. we must overcome 26, or however many, fragmented railway markets and create a single european railway area. this is european added value if we can do it, and i think we will do it. it may take longer, but it will happen. we hear from both passengers and businesses – industry, shippers, retailers – that to use railways, they need more attractive, efficient, cross-border and customer-oriented services. despite the three previous rail packages, technical rules and procedures are still fragmented and there are still obstacles to market entry. the fourth package takes a consistent approach in addressing these challenges: we must open markets de jure and eliminate regulatory, technical and administrative barriers de facto. we have proposed to make the european railway agency responsible for promoting interoperable technical rules and issuing safety certificates and vehicle authorisations that are valid throughout the eu. this will cut costs by about eur[nbsp ]500 million and reduce today’s lengthy procedures. it will benefit railways, but also the rail manufacturing industry that is so important for europe. for market opening to work, infrastructure managers should be strengthened and their independence guaranteed to ensure fair and non-discriminatory access to the network. clear governance rules, requirements on financial transparency and powerful regulators are essential conditions to make sure that gradual market opening delivers more efficient rail services with better quality and cost. competition is not an end in itself, but it is an important means to achieve better efficiency and quality of service. the commission proposal introduces the principle of mandatory competitive award of public service rail contracts, while preserving the ability of member states to define public service obligations. this is the best way to get the highest value for money out of the huge public sums spent on rail transport in europe today. you now have in front of you the compromises reached by the different rapporteurs. the commission would have been more ambitious in several important areas: tendering procedures for public service contracts in rail have been postponed to 2022, with even longer transitional periods; more possibilities are envisaged for direct award of rail contracts; separation requirements have been significantly softened and delegated to national regulators; the commission’s implementing powers have been significantly reduced. vested interests are at stake here. i am also fully aware that parliament has been under intense pressure from some incumbents who want to protect their historic markets in different ways. however, we should not forget that there are also many other parties with an interest in railways – freight operators, customers, manufacturers, new market entrants and, of course, passengers – who need them to become more efficient. and i strongly believe that more efficient railways also mean more traffic and therefore more jobs and opportunities for rail workers. so i would like to appeal to you to give the railway sector the boost it deserves. this requires important reforms and the political courage to overcome purely national interests. but it will be to the benefit of passengers, rail staff, taxpayers and – since rail is a relatively clean form of transport – ultimately also the environment.

in writing. with the adoption of the so-called fourth railway package, comprising as many as six legislative acts, including the single european railway area, national rail passenger services, interoperability of the rail system, railway safety, european union railway agency and standardisation of railway company accounting, i look forward to further harmonisation of the rules across the european union, improvement of the quality of the services provided and a reduction in administrative costs within the rail sector. in analysing the legislative package under discussion, the estimates of the increase in the number of jobs or the expected fall in the price of services in the railway sector due to increased competition were not unimportant for my vote. the vote on these matters was also important to me in the context of the long-running negotiations on the exclusion from the directive of undertakings operating on lines of less than 500 km. i welcome its outcome, which reflects an understanding of the need to ensure the right conditions for highly profitable businesses providing employment in regions with high unemployment.
in writing. by voting on the so-called fourth railway package, we are seeking to improve the situation of the railway sector across europe. we want to improve the competitiveness of railways in the member states, make it easier for new entrants to use the infrastructure and improve the quality of service. the rules that have been in place for many years, contained in previous railway packages, are designed to create a single railway market across the eu. this is to be achieved by liberalising the sector and allowing new operators to enter the market. a railway infrastructure authorisation is required. the proposed provisions concern, inter alia, the strengthening of the border between infrastructure managers and carriers (the so-called chinese wall), which is already implemented to some extent in some countries but may restrict the opening of the market to foreign carriers in others. the reasonable approach is to maintain existing public services, especially those which are not necessarily economically viable but which are often necessary for local residents. excessive liberalisation must not be allowed to result in the closure of all low-income lines and investment in only profitable services. in order to take account of their specificity, small railway structures (such as the pkp lhs) which are not of strategic importance in the european context should be excluded from the list. the aim of simplifying administrative procedures, such as those related to the certification of vehicles and personnel, is naturally a good idea, relieving the burden on service providers and concentrating responsibility on the european railway agency.

mr. chairman, please! for passengers and drivers, the name ecall should become synonymous with increased safety in the car. the ecall system can save lives and parliament has long called for its full implementation. thousands of people die in accidents, and more than 1.5 million were injured in 2012 alone. the system will alert the relevant services even if the driver is unconscious or seriously injured and cannot call for help on his own. the system will improve the efficiency of the emergency services by reducing their response time by up to 40% and in some cases by 50%. that is why it is so important that the system is accessible to all drivers. it is also important to note that the system has development potential for companies, as they will have the opportunity to provide the technology, parts and services needed for the operation of the ecall system. maintaining competitiveness and thus ensuring consumer choice is a very important issue from the internal market point of view. it's about the openness of the system. while it should obviously be used primarily to improve road safety, it cannot be excluded that its potential could be extended to other applications. in this respect, the european commission should examine what additional services could be included in the system as part of it and which would provide added value for passengers and drivers. the introduction of the system in all vehicles in the european union should significantly increase road safety and the october 2015 deadline for the implementation of the system should therefore be respected. the member states also have an important role to play in this area and should be more active and ambitious in their approach.

mr. chairman, please! the full implementation and efficient operation of the ecall mechanism will significantly mitigate the consequences of accidents. the commission's data show that this service will reduce the response time of the emergency services by up to 50%, which significantly increases the chances of victims in the event of a life-threatening event. the introduction of this alarm device into general use therefore takes into account a very important social interest. at the same time, i would like to call for more action to ensure the full roll-out of the 112 service. at present, there is still insufficient awareness of its functioning and the mechanism itself does not always work efficiently. a wide-ranging information campaign combined with a series of actions to improve the use of this tool would certainly be desirable.
in writing. – an in-vehicle ecall system is a service triggered either automatically or manually in the case of a car crash. it establishes a link to the emergency call centre and can speed up emergency response time by 40% to 50% of cases. according to estimates, it could save up to 2[nbsp ]500 lives a year. regardless the benefits of this service, currently only about 0.7% of vehicles in the eu are equipped with private ecall systems. the current report supports the deployment of the interoperable eu-wide ecall throughout the eu by october, 2015. it further backs the european commission’s proposal to ensure member states upgrade their infrastructure so that ecalls are efficiently passed on to emergency services. additionally, while taking into consideration the widespread deployment of gnss location technologies, the report emphasises the need to ensure ‘normal’ 112 calls are appropriately treated, next to ecalls. this will allow all citizens to benefit from the service, not only those who are equipped with ecall-enabled vehicles. considering that in 2012 alone, about 1.1m traffic accidents were registered on eu roads resulting in 28[nbsp ]000 deaths and more than 1.5m injuries, the current report is essential for increasing road safety standards across the eu.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the implementation of the ecall system across europe is an important step towards improving road safety. eu citizens can be sure that this system will significantly reduce the time taken by emergency services to respond to road accidents. the ecall system will be mandatory in new vehicles from 2015. e-call will be available to all citizens in europe as a pan-european service. the ecall system will be available free of charge to all car users on the basis of the 112 emergency telephone number. the report adopted in tomorrow's vote will ensure that cars equipped with ecall will not be able to be tracked continuously. the data sent from the system to the emergency centre will be limited to, among other things, the type of vehicle, the type of fuel, the time of the incident, the exact location of the car, the direction of travel and the number of passengers. i would like to thank the european commission very much for the initiative and encourage member states, telecommunications operators and vehicle manufacturers to get involved in the process of implementing the pan-european ecall system.

the next item is the report drawn up on behalf of the committee on legal affairs by klaus-heiner lehne and luigi berlinguer on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common european rules on sales (com ((2011) [nbsp ]0635 - c7-0329/2011 - 2011/0284 (cod)) (a7-0301/2013).
the deputy rapporteur. - mr. president, i'm not going to let you do this. i am the first to speak today, not because i am the rapporteur, but on behalf of my colleague and friend klaus-heiner lehne, who unfortunately cannot be here today for personal reasons. in the course of the many meetings and debates we have had in the european parliament on the establishment of a new mechanism for the legal regime for crossborder sales contracts, we have come to the conclusion that this instrument is absolutely essential for the common single market. it is intended to be an impetus for change on the community market. we are aware that there are people and companies who oppose this proposal or this solution, but the arguments in favour of it are clear. the work of the legal affairs committee, which has been ongoing since 2011, has generated a lot of excitement among both consumers and business representatives. it is understandable that every new instrument raises certain concerns, and i would like to dispel some of them on behalf of both mr lehne and myself. first, the new legal regime proposed by the rapporteurs concerns crossborder distance contracts. this slightly narrower scope of the regulation is primarily intended to provide an opportunity to overcome barriers to online shopping. secondly, it is to be an optional instrument, which means that both the consumer and the trader can choose whether they want to use this instrument on the basis of the community rules we are proposing or whether they prefer to stick to the solutions that apply in national systems. it should be made clear that the european sales law does not replace national law, but is merely an optional, additional version that can be chosen and that both parties to the transaction should agree to. if, on the other hand, one of the parties does not wish to agree to such a formula, the contract shall not take effect. the second issue, which is perhaps the most emotional, is the level of consumer protection proposed by the single european sales agreement. first of all, the consumer's consent to the conclusion of the contract cannot be presumed. it must be factual and clearly stated. before the final conclusion of the contract, consumers will be required to be informed of their rights under the single european sales agreement, but this information will also cover the consequences of concluding the contract on community terms. and that's the difference with the current rules in the individual member states. in fact, only five countries in the european union have such a level of information. of course, opponents of this optional solution will point out that full harmonisation of the rules or a change of the document from a regulation to a directive would yield better results. i do not agree with this approach and i believe that at the stage we are at today, only the adoption of this document which is being proposed today can make it possible to take a step forward to change the situation on the community market, to develop trade by enabling the development of trade on the net. the instrument we are proposing to you today is the best solution. i remember the enthusiasm of commissioner viviane reding at the first ministerial meeting when we discussed this issue in sopot, poland, in 2011, and the enthusiasm with which most ministers approached this option, and i am pleased that today we can finalise this very project that we started in 2011.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the common european sales rules aim to create uniform standards governing the union's internal market and to address the problems caused by the divergences between national contract law rules. this will create a new online marketing tool that also provides greater protection for consumers shopping online. i support the idea of making this instrument optional, and only covering those companies and consumers who see real benefits. the legislation proposed in this report will only apply to businesses that carry out cross-border transactions, especially online, by proposing uniform rules, reducing costs and facilitating compliance checks. i agree with the rapporteurs that this ground-breaking initiative will significantly facilitate the development of cross-border trade, improving the situation of consumers and businesses operating in the new digital trading environment. moreover, by reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens, european legislation will become an effective tool in achieving a well-functioning internal market. i congratulate both rapporteurs on their ambitious report.
the deputy rapporteur. - mr. president, i'm not going to let you do this. i would like to thank the commissioner very warmly for having understood this idea, which has been the rapporteur's and the european parliament's concern. to make a step forward sometimes means taking a step back from some proposals, which does not mean, commissioner, that we will not come back to your proposal in the future to extend these new solutions even further. i hope that mr fox is satisfied with the explanations that the commissioner has given. there is no contradiction between strengthening the position of small and mediumsized enterprises through this optional form of the european sales law and protecting consumer rights more than in many cases exists today in the member states. imagine, mr fox, that today the buyer - the customer - very often has no choice about what form of compensation to take for a defective service or for a defective product. in this optional formula which we are proposing today and which i hope the european parliament will adopt by a large majority, such a possibility exists. i could give many more examples to show that this optional solution is a step forward, and i can even imagine that in the future this optional solution will override the national law based contract. i would ask everyone to support this report so that the european parliament can once again sign up to this formula of helping small and mediumsized enterprises and all european consumers.

president of the czech republic. - mr[nbsp ] president, every politician who speaks in the european parliament expresses, tacitly or openly, his european dream, so let me follow that good tradition. first however, i want to tell you what my european dream is not. i am inspired here by a well-known polish philosopher, leszek kolakowski, who gave a lecture, i guess in 1957, under the title ‘what is socialism?’ and started by saying, ‘comrades, i was asked to tell what socialism is. very well, but first i will tell you what socialism is not. socialism, comrades, is not the murder of political opponents, socialism is not concentration camps, socialism is not political prisoners, socialism is not censorship ...’ and he continued in that vein for more than half an hour. i can tell you in just five minutes what my european dream is not. i should add first though that, at the end of his lecture, kolakowski said, ‘now, comrades, i will tell you what socialism is: socialism, comrades, is a good thing.’ and that was all. so now, in five minutes, i will tell you what my european dream is not. my european dream does not include the crazy movement of the european parliament from strasbourg to brussels and back. dream is, and i shall start by quoting another philosopher – czech this time – václav bělohradský, who said that european citizenship was a ‘cultural choice’. i agree with him. we were all born somewhere, and that is not to our credit, but the cultural choice for european citizenship is a choice made of our own free will and is valid and useful, particularly in a complicated situation such as we have today. let us define what it means. culture, firstly, is more than cold economic calculation, comparing losses and benefits. culture is a set of common rules of behaviour, and what we need in an integration process is to start with common rules – or equal rules, if you wish, which are not the same as equal levels. what is the difference? the common rule is, for instance, the relationship between the minimum wage and the average wage, but the levels of those wages depend on labour productivity. levels cannot be regulated by common principles. however, we need common rules in many areas of european policy. let us start with foreign policy. henry kissinger’s ironic question ‘who do i call if i want to speak to europe?’ is still valid. there is still no common foreign as soon as possible. those who criticise the euro suffer from what i would call a fear of the unknown. i think the euro has been a stabilising factor for economic development. more than that, however, in writing. - the single european act gave the european union's internal market a community dimension, which was further strengthened by the maastricht treaty of 1992 and the amsterdam treaty of 1997. the vast majority of decisions taken by the eu council on internal market issues are taken by qualified majority. derogations from this rule concern in particular tax policy, the movement of persons and the interests and rights of workers. the idea of a single market without internal national borders is based on a high level of mutual trust and on the equivalence of regulatory systems. any significant failure to apply the common rules in any part of the single market puts the rest of the system at risk and undermines its integrity. the european commission is therefore obliged to keep a close eye on compliance by all market participants and has been given the means to enforce the rules against member state governments that do not show the necessary level of discipline. the european court of justice is the final instance in this respect.

in writing. - the work carried out by local authorities and ngos is an invaluable tool in the implementation of not only the europe 2020 strategy, but also many other objectives of building a common, solidary but dynamically developing europe. the report shows that not all countries or regions are doing equally well in implementing cohesion policy programmes. some are struggling, especially with the latest technology, internet access, and transportation infrastructure. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european network of regional authorities is based on the principle of subsidiarity. i would like to support the report, particularly in the area of job creation policy. after such a great crisis, the most important thing is to try to rebuild the economy and help society to recover from this sad experience. programmes that support primarily small and medium-sized enterprises, the main drivers of services and industry are therefore important and will have a positive impact on economic recovery.
in writing. - cohesion policy is a strategic policy, essential to bridging the gap between the more and less developed regions of the union as a whole. cohesion policy programmes will have to select investment priorities, taking into account the starting point of a region or city, in relation to the national 2020 objectives, identifying which activities to promote and which to combat. future cohesion programmes will therefore have to place particular emphasis on incentives, growth and investment in job creation for a stable recovery and to reduce unemployment, especially among young people.
in writing. - this report assesses how, in the context of cohesion policy, regions and cities can contribute to the three types of growth envisaged by the europe 2020 strategy. the european parliament report states that cohesion policy programmes should choose their investment priorities taking into account the starting position of the region or city in relation to the national 2020 targets. cohesion policy programmes are an opportunity to create a comprehensive development strategy that is targeted to specific needs and reflects the trade-offs and interdependencies between different types of investment, which translates into more efficient use of resources and faster development of regions and cities.
in writing. - the union's territories, thousands of kilometres from the continent, are in a difficult situation. this makes integration with the community and contact with the country to which the territory belongs difficult. supporting these areas is not only our duty, but also a long-term investment. the eu institutions are now ignoring these territories, repeatedly not including them on maps of the union. the community is based on solidarity and helping the weak. i would like to draw particular attention to the difficult situation of agriculture in the outermost regions. i mean the structure of the farms and the limited market. to support development, domestic production should be encouraged by replacing imports. we need to tap into the potential of both the exotic and the original culture that exists there, offering unique goods. it is also necessary to protect them by keeping in mind protected and reserved designations of origin and local indications. of course, it's not just agriculture and food that are the locomotives for the most remote areas. coordinated action based on eu strategies is needed to ensure that these regions develop properly. the sources of potential are endless, and with a report like this, we can do a lot of good for those areas.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the employment policies of the member states. one of the objectives of the european union, as set out in article 145 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, is to pursue a uniform employment strategy in all member states, with a view to continuously improving the skills of citizens. this is particularly important in the face of the enormous challenges facing europe today. i am thinking in particular of the deepening demographic and economic problems, which have as a direct consequence high levels of unemployment, especially among young people, as well as the growing problem of poverty and social exclusion. in response to these challenges, the european union adopted in 2010 a new 'europe 2020' strategy for sustainable development and employment, which supports actions to boost growth and create jobs. i believe that only joint and integrated action by all member states, which actively implement and promote the guidelines for european employment policy, can prevent the economic and social problems that are increasing in europe.
in writing. - the biggest problem facing europe today is not the economic crisis. and it's not climate change, and it's not poor competitiveness in global trade. the biggest challenge we face today is demographic change and youth unemployment in europe. across europe, we have a negative trend in natural growth and population ageing, which is particularly evident among the new member states. this is due to low birth rates and the emigration of the younger generation. we have very good education systems, more and more people are getting higher education, and yet the unemployment rate among graduates is very high. this is partly the result of educational profiles that are not adapted to the needs of the market: most young europeans have a humanities education, while there is a shortage of science professionals on the labour market. creating jobs for young people is an absolute priority. the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states established by council decision 2010/707/ec are intended, inter alia, to increase employment among age groups, to review tax and social benefit systems, to promote gender equality in the labour market, to promote active ageing and the integration of young people, the disabled, migrants and other groups at risk of exclusion. therefore, this framework should also apply in 2014, as recommended by the author.
in writing. - value added tax covers all types of commercial activity, the production and distribution of goods and the provision of services. it does not concern exported goods or services, but imported goods or services. this is very important for union producers to be able to compete on equal terms within the internal market with suppliers of imported goods and services that are established outside the union. vat issues are very important for businesses and the lack of appropriate regulation can lead to the creation of burdensome barriers. this is the case, for example, in the case of tax reporting obligations, where the diversity of vat returns in different member states places a heavy burden on companies operating across borders. the commission has therefore proposed the introduction of a standard vat return, which will reduce administrative formalities and related costs for both member states' tax authorities and taxpayers. the standardisation of the information required in the vat return, as well as its electronic format, will make it easier for companies to provide the tax authorities of the member states in which they operate with the information necessary for the purposes of vat control and collection. this will mean saving time, reducing costs, allowing easy correction of errors and thus maintaining a balance between the need to reduce the burden on business and the need to remove obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. - unfortunately, turkey remains the most important country for the transit of illegal immigrants into the union. this is often done at great risk to life. for example, people attempting to enter greece use freight transport, including sometimes refrigerated cars. there are also known cases of travel on chassis elements or other external vehicle installations. the curious solution is to blame the driver, who in most cases was not even aware that he was transporting the immigrant. i hope that this agreement and similar agreements with third countries will at least reduce the most dangerous forms of transfer of citizens across the community's borders.
mr. chairman, please! rail transport remains an important means of transporting people. while modern, high-speed connections between large agglomerations are common in the countries of the old union, in poland the quality of rail services still does not meet consumers' expectations. particular problems arise during periods of increased tourism, for example during christmas and holiday travel. the infrastructure is also still inadequate, resulting in regular delays and cancellations. in the interests of polish passengers, i would like to ask the relevant european institutions to be more involved in cooperation on the development of rail transport in my country, which is implemented in a significant part with the use of eu funds. for example, the modernisation of the kraków-katowice key line was once again postponed and the funds transferred to other purposes.
in writing. - i voted against amendment no 5 proposed by the committee on transport and tourism, which points to the positive impact of the opening up of the rail passenger market on the growth of this market and the quality of services in countries such as sweden and the united kingdom. it was based on unbelievable opinions and research. because of the lack of voting discipline in our political group, it is a good indicator that none of the british members of the epp group supported this amendment either. furthermore, the markets in sweden and the united kingdom cannot be representative of the community as a whole. the economies of these countries are much more developed than those of the new community countries and the opening of the railway market may therefore bring about changes other than those envisaged.
in writing. - there are currently over 11 000 different national technical and safety rules for rail in the 28 member states of the european union. this contributes to significant distortions of competition and excessive administrative costs. further harmonisation of rail and the creation of a single european railway area with common rules on the governance of railway undertakings and infrastructure managers, infrastructure financing and charges for its use, conditions for access to rail infrastructure and services and regulatory oversight of the railway market is essential if the railway is to become a credible alternative to other modes of transport in terms of price and quality. the new railway package aims to strengthen passenger rights and guarantee the right to free movement. in the vote on the document i also supported the amendment relating to small railway structures existing in poland, germany, the czech republic, etc., concerning the possibility of excluding from the scope of the directive undertakings operating on lines of less than 500 km.
in writing. - i strongly support the outcome of the vote. i am especially content that my introduction of an amendment (87) for plenary excluding the lhs (linia kolejowa nr 65) rail connection in poland from any legal requirements concerning the institutional separation succeeded. for this technically unique line (different gauge from the polish standard gauge), which stretches 400 km from the bug river bridge (polish-ukraine border) to slawkow (silesian voivodeship), a separation of infrastructure manager and railway operator would create an administrative burden putting the operating efficiency at danger.
in writing. - the report you presented raises a number of questions. when we discuss the rail package, it is worth remembering that the rail sector is in a prolonged crisis. trains are losing out to cars and planes. the recipe i'm proposing is wrong. the situation in rail transport will not improve if the only remedy is to liberalise and privatise the european market. two other factors are underestimated in this report. first, there is a need for professionalism on the railways and for more professional stability for staff. europe's railways should be run by professionals. today, too often, they are replaced by financiers whose only criterion of evaluation is economic efficiency. they forget that the railway has an important public mission to fulfill. the second problem is railway safety. in recent years, there have been too many tragic disasters, like the szczecin in poland or the viareggio in spain. it's also the result of a constant search for savings. you can't afford to skimp on the safety of your passengers.
in writing. - amendment no 72 proposed by saïda el khadraoui to recital 11 of the draft report contrary to the commission proposal takes account of the manner and extent of the provision of social protection to public service workers. the commission text does not ensure proper enforcement. it states the problem, it postulates the solution, but it does not specify who and how is responsible for enforcing the provision. the amendment specifies measures to protect employees of companies that do not win contracts through tendering. the amendment introduced assumes that competition cannot have the effect of worsening working conditions. it is intended to protect workers' wages, which may be unduly reduced by lower prices for services. the amendment corrects the shortcomings in the commission's text, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - as a responsible mep for the socialists and democrats (s&d) on this report in the european parliament i was able to defend the workers’ rights and a balanced approach when it comes to competition. in case of changes between railway operators, we managed to include the mandatory transferral of staff so that social protection and efficient competition can co-exist. whereas the european commission wanted to force the member states to public tender every railway service in poland, we secured the option of well-balanced direct award of public service obligation contracts by the competent authorities. i fully support this report and voted in favour.
mr. chairman, please! the report by mr cramer on railway safety is a very important report. travellers in the community are looking above all for a fast, cheap and safe means of transport. on the other hand, railway companies are looking for profits and rolling stock manufacturers want to bring their vehicles to market as soon as possible. i hope that through the whole railway package we will respond to the needs of these parties and develop the potential of the railway market in the european union, which in many member states, including my own country, poland, is under-invested but also constrained by administrative procedures.
in writing. - rail is one of the safest modes of transport, but further action is needed to ensure even better protection of passengers, human life, public health and the environment. ensuring railway safety requires comprehensive action and cooperation between many actors railway undertakings, infrastructure managers, the railway industry and safety authorities, and the specification of the responsibilities of each actor within their respective areas of activity. it is therefore particularly important to continue the process of harmonising safety rules so that all passengers in the eu are adequately protected. the railway safety rules adopted should also take into account appropriate procedures and tools for the information, management and response to emergencies, as well as for the investigation of accidents.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important report since it deals with technical aspects in relation to safety issues which allow more efficient, and simplified and harmonised authorisation and certification procedures for railway companies. these changes will ensure common safety rules in the 26 member states of the european union operating railways.
mr. chairman, please! i strongly support the proposal to introduce a reporting obligation on possible incidents that threaten aircraft. the principle of mutual trust underlying the regulation will bring greater transparency to the sector as a whole. historic aircraft and amateur construction are excluded from the regulation, which will avoid unnecessary regulatory burdens. taking into account the increase in air travel in europe, the analysis of hazard and incident data should help to reduce the number of accidents.
mr. chairman, please! we have debated the details of this regulation at committee level on many occasions. i support the recognition of ecall as a free public service. i particularly welcome the fact that this system is based on a publicly available, interoperable platform, open to the introduction of possible additional services in the future. this will complement the voluntary ecall system developed by some member states. the mandatory on-board system will provide significant added value for road users, allowing emergency services to reach victims of accidents more quickly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal to make the use of ecall in new vehicles compulsory. this platform, which is to be mandatory from october 2015 in cars in the european union, will be based on approved on-board devices that connect to the european emergency number 112. this will be a public and free system, which will most likely also allow the installation of additional systems or on-board applications in the future. it should be borne in mind that the use of the pan-european ecall platform will rely on the processing of data such as the location or identification of the vehicle, and therefore, in order to ensure an adequate level of protection of personal data of drivers, the system should be passive, without the possibility of tracking vehicles. i believe that this service will directly contribute to saving lives. it will enable emergency services to arrive at the scene of an accident in a reasonable time, reducing the number of fatalities and thus ensuring a much higher level of safety on european roads.
in writing. - parliament has long called for the full implementation of ecall, which will significantly improve road safety. thousands of people are killed in accidents, and more than 1.5 million were injured in 2012 alone. the system will alert the relevant services even if the driver is unconscious or seriously injured and cannot call for help on his own. the system will improve the efficiency of the emergency services by reducing their response time considerably. that is why it is so important that the system is accessible to all drivers. maintaining competitiveness and thus ensuring consumer choice is a very important issue from the internal market point of view. it's a matter of openness. while it should obviously be used primarily to improve road safety, it cannot be excluded that its potential could be extended to other applications. in this respect, the european commission should examine what additional services could be included in the system and which would provide added value for passengers and drivers. it is also important to note that the system has development potential for companies, as they will have the opportunity to provide the technology, parts and services needed to operate the system. the introduction of the system in all vehicles in the european union should significantly increase road safety and the october 2015 deadline for the implementation of the system should therefore be respected.
in writing. - the eu has always been strongly committed to reducing the number of road accidents and mitigating their consequences when they occur. for these reasons, the european parliament adopted the ecall project by an overwhelming majority. the new instrument, once it enters into force in a mandatory form, will reduce the number of fatalities and the severity of injuries resulting from road accidents by allowing the emergency services to intervene more quickly at the scene of the accident. by october 2015, all new models of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles will be equipped with this system and the necessary infrastructure will be established for the proper reception and handling of calls in order to ensure compatibility, interoperability and continuity of the ecall service at eu level.
in writing. - in the event of a serious road accident, an ecall-equipped vehicle will automatically call the emergency number of the nearest accident reporting point and send a message. this allows emergency calls to be made without language barriers and can significantly contribute to reducing the number of road fatalities in europe. ecall reduces waiting times for help and can save around 2 500 lives in the european union every year, as well as tens of thousands of serious injuries. the introduction of a public eu vehicle alarm system is an important step towards improving road safety.

in writing. - the number of websites is growing rapidly, and they are increasingly used to provide information or services. the same applies to public and private sector entities. the public sector already has hundreds of thousands of websites, but less than 10% of websites in the eu meet the standards for web accessibility. this area is home to thousands of businesses, generating jobs and a turnover of €144 billion. network accessibility can contribute to the further development of the single market and to ensuring universal access to services for all eu citizens. the accessibility of the network is of great economic importance and has a significant potential for economic growth and social inclusion. in particular, the use of websites by all citizens, including people with disabilities. therefore, all public sector bodies should apply the principle of network availability. member states have already implemented legislation on this issue, but barriers remain due to differences in national approaches. the new rules therefore aim to approximate the member states' rules on the accessibility of public sector bodies' websites by setting out harmonised requirements. one of the more important aspects is to identify the types of public sector bodies' websites that are relevant to citizens' participation in economic and social life.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! i voted today in favour of the report on the accessibility of public sector websites because i believe that the internet is an increasingly common tool for the pursuit of broadly defined public policy objectives. it is gradually becoming not only the main channel for the flow of information between public administrations and citizens, but also a tool for the delivery of a specific service. the rapid digitization of recent years has created a phenomenon that we can call modern illiteracy. digital backwardness is increasingly becoming a cause of social exclusion. undoubtedly, this is partly due to the fact that only 10% of websites meet the minimum standards for web accessibility. that is why the initiative of the european commission and the comments made by the rapporteur are so important. the issue of accessibility of websites is also important from the point of view of the labour market and free access to information on employment conditions, especially abroad. i have personally fought for this in working on the new directive on the posting of workers.
in writing. - the economic crisis has led to a sharp decline in the confidence of citizens in banking institutions and a reluctance of the latter to take the risks associated with lending and credit. as a result, much investment and economic growth in the member states has been held back. to enable economic growth, business development and financial stability in europe, we need alternative financing methods, especially long-term financing. institutional schemes such as pension funds can potentially provide long-term investment, while development banks such as the european investment bank can support the development of private enterprise. additional financing for smes can be obtained by increasing the credit capacity of the european investment fund and by implementing provisions simplifying administrative procedures, as for example the framework programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises. i agree with the committee on employment and social affairs that funding the eu economy should be in the public interest. we need to support job creation, strengthen social cohesion and tackle exclusion. let us also not forget that it is often investments in economically 'non-viable' sectors, such as education and research, that will lead to better quality of life and economic prosperity in the long run.

question no 2: what is the position of the european commission on the legal status of the part of the fisheries protection zone in the svalbard region which lies east of the line drawn in murmansk? is this part to be considered as international waters off the russian shelf or is it part of the russian exclusive economic zone? thirdly, if european union fishermen lose their fishing rights in the svalbard fisheries protection zone east of the murmansk line, will the commission consider their claims for compensation? fourthly, what is the commission's position on the legality of the transfer of responsibility by norway and russia for part of the norwegian exclusive economic zone in the barents sea? in writing. - crossborder trade between businesses and consumers is an important aspect of the internal market. the common european sales rules are intended to be an independent and uniform set of rules designed, inter alia, to protect consumers. however, these provisions do not replace national regulations but constitute an optional regime of contract law. it is certainly necessary that this system be clear and precise and also consistent with existing legislation, in particular with regard to consumer rights. for these reasons, the internal market committee played a significant role in the report, paying attention, inter alia, to the position of the consumer as a party to the contract, which is by nature much weaker than that of the firm. consumers therefore require a high level of protection. however, the proposed rules are intended to be optional, which creates legal uncertainty rather than clarity for consumers. the imco commission has thus challenged this system, although it is convinced of the need for common european regulations in the field of consumer contract law. a possible alternative to the optional right to buy and sell could be further harmonisation of eu consumer contract law and the development of online commerce by regulating digital content contracts. the report should provide a basis for possible further negotiations with the council on this issue, and the priority should remain to ensure legal clarity and a high level of consumer protection.
in writing. - the regulations adopted under the tobacco directive are the result of a long negotiation process and a compromise taking into account both health arguments and the reasons of the tobacco industry, including poland, as one of the largest tobacco producers in europe. the final text regulates, among other things, a six-year transitional period for menthol cigarettes, allows the use of sugar during production, while prohibiting other flavourings (except smokeless tobacco products), does not ban slim cigarettes, requires the use of 65% of the surface of cigarette packaging for health warnings, and takes into account the implementation of control systems by member states to prevent illicit smuggling or verify the age of the person making the purchase. the compromise also addressed the issue of e-cigarettes and allowed for their widespread availability, while reserving the member states' discretion for further detailed decisions. in the context of the preliminary proposal of the european commission, whose provisions i considered inadequate, i accept the outcome of the european parliament's work as balanced, as it takes into account not only health policy issues but also eliminates negative consequences for production and employment in poland.
in writing. - the report adopted today is the result of many months of very intensive work. the aim remained to ensure a high level of consumer protection and in particular to reduce the attractiveness of tobacco products to children and young people. data indicate that as many as 70 percent of smokers have smoked their first cigarette before the age of 18. tobacco-related diseases kill 700 000 people in the eu every year. this is why it was so important to introduce legislation to ensure that consumers are provided with reliable information about the effects of tobacco products on human health. i therefore supported mixed health warnings in the form of colour photographs and text that will be more visible and readable to consumers. i also advocated keeping slim and menthol cigarettes on the market for a long transitional period because if we are not banning all cigarettes, banning only one type of tobacco product will not reduce the number of smokers and may have a negative impact on the economy. from the very beginning of the very difficult work on the directive, i have stressed the need to balance the interests of producers and health issues. i am glad that after many months of talks, meetings, persuading other members to accept the polish position and, as a result, my opinion in the imco committee, the idea of keeping slimes and menthols on the market has been considered. the compromise adopted is balanced and beneficial for consumers and producers.
in writing. - an anti-nicotine campaign cannot be based solely on actions targeting manufacturers. this is not the way to end smoking. but our job is to protect citizens as best we can, and that's why we need to take steps to raise awareness and educate the public about the dangers of smoking. certainly, part of this campaign is to reduce the appeal of the habit, to ban colourful packaging and neat packaging. will this help you stop smoking? and are these actions legal in the context of competition and free market laws? if so, why don't we standardize the whiskey and wine bottles? after all, drunk driving, drug abuse, and post-drink violence are not isolated incidents. i think there is a certain injustice to the tobacco industry. but i would like to support the idea of fighting this horrible, senseless addiction that causes so much irreversible damage and deadly disease. i therefore support any action to educate citizens, especially young people, about the harmfulness of nicotine and to oblige manufacturers to label products correctly and to provide consumers with accurate information.
in writing. - the work on the shape of the new tobacco products directive has been controversial. and rightly so, because first of all, smoking remains a serious social problem, with implications for public health. secondly, as i have argued many times, the european commission's initial legislative proposal could not be accepted by countries such as poland. today we have another document, which has been substantially amended. through our joint efforts, we have been able to reach a compromise that i believe balances the interests of public health and those of workers in the tobacco industry and trade. first, the new appearance and shape of tobacco packaging will no longer leave consumers in any doubt that these products pose a serious health risk. we will withdraw menthol cigarettes from the market, but after a six-year transition period to allow for market adjustments. we also managed to preserve the slim cigarettes that are popular in poland and to secure the use of sugar as a technological additive. finally, e-cigarette users can rest easy, as these products will not have to be subject to pharmaceutical regulation, with their quality being determined by special regulations. so we're not dumping the baby with the bathtub. protecting the health of eu citizens and raising their awareness of the effects of smoking will not have a negative impact on thousands of workers in the sector. that is why i can vote for the report this time.
in writing. - i have voted in favor of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states concerning the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products (com(2012)0788 – c7-0420/2012 – 2012/0366(cod)). as many may know, this report was surrounded by controversy and heated debate. my perspective is that the legislation serves it purpose of minimising the attractiveness of smoking for minors and provides the needed information regarding the health risks involved in the use of tobacco products. while i do not condone nor condemn the use of tobacco, the health risks are there and our citizens deserve to know what effects it may have. while, at the same time, a ban or restriction on said products to those who are of age should not be implemented as it also restricts freedoms as well as increases other issues such as black market demand, which the eu has little or no power to regulate. this directive allows the tobacco user to continue to use tobacco and at the same time increases the protection for our young people not to obtain the habit.

in writing. - solvit allows for the resolution of international disputes through informal online appeals. through the cooperation of the member states' administrative units, it has already helped to resolve several thousand cases over its more than 10 years of operation. complaints lodged by citizens are most often of a private nature. they concern, for example, professional qualifications or the benefits to which they are entitled. the scheme is also used by businesses, most often in vat cases. however, the percentage of companies using solvit is still quite low. in the report we adopted, we advocate the widespread use of the system, calling on the european commission to promote it actively, especially among business circles. it is also necessary to harmonise single market rules, which in many member states are still incompatible with union law, which makes it impossible to solve the problem through the solvit platform. this tool has proved its worth. we should therefore continue to support its development. an effective solvit 2.0 will allow for the handling of a wider range of stakeholders as well as more complex cases.
in writing. - solvit is an online problem-solving network for citizens and businesses to address complaints about the misapplication of internal market rules. this report is the european parliament's response to the commission's recommendations on improving solvit. parliament's proposal focuses in particular on raising awareness among citizens and businesses of the existence and functioning of solvit, with particular attention to small and medium-sized enterprises. in addition, the working methods of the solvit centres should be improved, in particular as regards communication between the reporting agents and the centres. the report also encourages solvit centres to cooperate with each other, with a particular focus on standardising procedures and services for citizens and businesses.

in writing. - the european arrest warrant (eaw) is an important european legal instrument based on the mutual recognition principle, whereby judicial decisions are executed on the basis of mutual trust. the eaw ensures our open borders are not exploited, and suspects and accused persons are brought to justice through a faster and more efficient system. however, despite an overall positive evaluation, review reports presented by the european commission point to imperfections in the functioning of the system, especially with regard to the gaps in the eaw framework decision. i can personally testify to problems with the implementation of the eaw after having aided a polish mother whose child was kidnapped by his greek father in july 2013. in this case, even though an eaw was issued, the lack of communication and cooperation between police authorities in the two eu member states created obstacles to returning the child to his mother. over five months passed until they were reunited. the current report addresses many of the concerns and it asks the european commission to present a legislative proposal within one year to remedy them. reforming the operation of the eaw is an outmost priority for maintaining its credibility and functioning, and therefore i voted to support this report.

rapporteur. - mr president, this is the final annual committee on petitions (peti) report of the seventh legislature of the european parliament, so it is more than just an outline of the committee’s activities in 2013. it is also an overview of the whole parliamentary term. the basic document is divided into three parts. the first part details the work of the committee and the summary of our achievements. the second and third chapters, entitled new horizons and working methods, are basically proposals for new suggestions to make the committee’s work more substantial and visible. one of these is the emphasis on collaboration with the other eu institutions and national authorities. as we all know, peti is the platform for citizens to voice their concerns, and this enables dialogue. therefore, it is very important to adopt final internal rules and to revise accordingly the rules of procedure of the european parliament to improve peti working methods. furthermore, we need clear deadlines to speed up the life cycle of petitions, but we must not forget to make the whole process more transparent and democratic. among the most important tools of the peti committee are the fact-finding visits. the revision of the rules on these is needed to introduce more efficiency and facilitate organisation. this is what we have to accomplish in the next term. as for the past, in 2013 the petitions committee was responsible for the organisation of the election of the new ombudsman, ms emily o’reilly, and dealt with a relatively higher number of fact-finding visits than in the past. the peti committee held a series of public hearings on major subjects of petitions, such as citizenship and the importance of having single registration procedures for eu citizens in the national and european elections; the hearings on the impact of the economic crisis – petitioners here have criticised the unwillingness of banks to provide investment funding for small businesses – and the hearings on the rights of disabled people and, more precisely, of blind people. the conclusions seem clear: annual dialogue between the members of the peti committee and the members of the petitions committees in the national parliaments is needed. on top of that, there is a strong recommendation for the use of new information and video facilities for future peti committee meetings which will bring further cost savings in the organisation of its hearings. as for the statistics, since 2009 about 10[nbsp ]000 petitions have been registered in the european parliament, of which about 60[nbsp ]% were declared admissible. in 2013 alone, 2[nbsp ]800 petitions were registered. i am convinced that more and more europeans will address petitions to the european parliament in the future. we need to live up to their expectations and call on the european parliament to adopt urgent measures to ensure the efficient and transparent processing of petitions. this report should be viewed not only as an achievement but also as a stepping stone towards new reforms which would allow the petitions committee to further assist citizens and to set standards for the upcoming legislature.

in writing. - today's vote on the report gives the green light to launch the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in spain. the request concerns 300 exemptions in 198 small and medium-sized enterprises operating in the textile sector in the comunidad valenciana region during the period from 1 november 2012 to 1 august 2013. the egf funding (eur 840 000) will be used for a coordinated package of personalised services to help 300 redundant workers in the textile sector and to facilitate their reintegration into the labour market. the decreases were due to major structural changes in world trade linked to globalisation. this is the first mobilisation of the egf in 2014.
in writing. - the european globalisation adjustment fund will help companies making collective redundancies provide individual support for redundant workers. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is a financial support for redundant workers. the egf may provide financial resources for redundant workers. it is a financial instrument of the european union which was set up in 2006 to provide support to persons benefiting from exemptions resulting from major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation, where these exemptions have a significant impact on the regional or local economy. under the derogation until 31 december 2011, support may also be granted to workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis.
in writing. - the european commission proposes to replace the 12 existing legislative directives governing the production and distribution of plant reproductive material with a single regulation. the aim is to ensure that the material is of adequate quality and that users can make informed, rational choices when procuring it. unfortunately, the ec's plans are causing concern amongst those who use reproductive material. during the consultations, many member states have acknowledged that they are satisfied with the existing rules, as the specific nature of the use of reproductive material requires a very different approach in each case. moreover, replacing the provisions with a single act would most likely have a negative impact on small and medium-sized enterprises. in the committee on agriculture and rural development, we tabled over 1400 amendments to the draft report, drawing attention, among other things, to the european commission's idea that it could implement new legislative elements through delegated acts at a later stage. at a time when we do not know what the future regulations governing the market for reproductive material might look like, we are simply not able to accept such proposals. we are rational and listen to the voice of our citizens, and we therefore vote to reject the commission's proposal altogether.
in writing. - the draft regulation on the production and placing on the market of plant reproductive material presented by the european commission was far from what the public expected from the outset. today we have given a strong signal by rejecting the commission's legislative proposal. the material used for plant reproduction requires complex regulation. the rules are now scattered across dozens of different pieces of legislation, creating a patchwork of articles that make it difficult for users of reproductive material to work. however, i have doubts about the logic of consolidating these provisions in the form of a regulation. i believe that the european commission should present new regulations in the form of a directive, thus giving member states more room to implement appropriate solutions, given the specific nature of the use of reproductive material in a given country and the organisational structure of the institutions responsible for its supervision. finally, at the agri and envi committees, i persuaded a number of members to table together some 100 amendments to exclude forest reproductive material from the scope of the proposed regulation. it is important to know that in countries like poland in particular, the forestry sector is governed by different laws and processes reproductive material in a completely different way than agriculture. it also has efficient management and control systems in place. that's why i think it should be outside the scope of the law on reproductive material.
in writing. - a brief history of the draft regulation shows that the environment of farmers, hobbyists and environmental organisations can provide meps, who rarely deal with seeds on a daily basis, with sufficient factual arguments to make sensible decisions. however, the debate on seed regulation will not end soon, and the fight for the rights of small seed producers and the preservation of biodiversity will continue. i hope that the commission and the members of the european parliament will not go back to the ill-advised idea of regulating everything that is still natural, including seeds and farmers' rights to use them.
in writing. - the european commission recommends that the member states of the european union reduce administrative expenditure. however, the savings do not apply to the eu institutions, which are increasing employment even in times of crisis. the european commission employs the most people. the 27 directorates-general (which we can call the equivalent of ministries) employ almost 33 000 civil servants. in the area of economic affairs, employment has increased by almost one third since the start of the crisis. the largest increase in employment in the commission was in 2009 - 41%c. as employment increases, so does administrative expenditure. in 2008, eu bureaucracy cost €6.4 billion, and this year it is expected to cost €8.4 billion. half of that money is from the administration's payroll, which hasn't been cut since the crisis. the commission staff member's salary starts at eur 31 000 per year and can go up to eur 220 000. this is supplemented by an allowance of 16%, among others, of the basic equipment if the work requires a move.
in writing. - serbia, despite its history with the ottoman empire and its religious ties with russia, is a country closely linked to european civilization, so it is natural that a stabilisation and association agreement should be created between serbia and the eu. this is particularly important in the current geopolitical situation and during the crimean crisis. it is important that countries that are not yet members of the union feel the strength and support of the european union. we need to be more open and engaged to build a strong and secure europe. only then can we guarantee peace and development for the entire continent. the most important thing to consider is trade cooperation, which will be the best support for a country in crisis and still struggling with the echoes of war. these are our neighbors we have to take care of. otherwise, they'll look elsewhere for help.
in writing. - following the dayton peace agreement in 1995, the european union formulated its policy towards the western balkans. the commitment to rebuild the region, to work to overcome tensions and conflicts and to integrate the western balkans into european integration processes was declared. from the outset, the so-called regional approach, agreed by the eu general affairs council in february 1996, has been an important element of eu policy. this meant that the european union would not differentiate its policy towards the individual balkan states, but would primarily encourage them to improve their relations with each other, especially in the political, economic and social spheres. however, the assumptions adopted have not become the basis for an effective eu policy. in addition, the events in kosovo in 1999, the gradual reduction of us and nato involvement in the balkans and the ineffectiveness of humanitarian aid have led to the need to develop new solutions. the stability pact for south-eastern europe was signed on 10 june 1999 and involves more than 40 countries, including the european commission, nato, the osce and the g8. its main objectives are: to initiate a process of systemic transformation in the region, to establish good neighbourly relations between the countries of the region, to shape civil society, to develop economic cooperation based on market economy principles and to remove restrictions on trade. the european union has taken direct control of the implementation of the principles of the pact.
in writing. - the question of appropriate harmonisation of legislation is of the utmost importance. the introduction of consistent technical rules should only concern those areas where it is essential to achieve the objectives set out in those rules. the european council, in its conclusions of june 2009, endorsed the establishment of a single rulebook for financial services, to which regulations and implementing technical standards should also contribute. as regards technical standards, it should also be ensured that supervisory experts are involved in the process of their development and evaluation, given the need to draw on their expertise. not all requirements in union legislative acts are fully harmonised, and many are not in line with the precautionary principle. they therefore require additional time and attention, as does the specification of the conditions for the application of certain requirements. it is necessary to seek to eliminate situations where they constitute an obstacle for member states for whatever reason, for example in terms of access to additional information. more stringent requirements are not in themselves a more reliable and accurate solution. regulations and implementing technical standards should, on the other hand, clearly define the scope for action by member states in specific areas and indicate clearly whether discretion is provided for and allowed therein.
in writing. - the new year of 2014 has been a boom for the european union's banking system. this year will mark a historic milestone the european central bank will start to exercise banking supervision over credit institutions based in the euro area. i am attaching a diagram below which shows, of course in a very simplified way, the location and shape of european banking supervision. the european system of financial supervisors (esfs) comprises the competent supervisory authorities of the member states and three supervisory authorities responsible for supervising the three segments of the eu financial market. the european banking authority (eba), the european securities and markets authority and the european insurance and occupational pensions authority are the latter. they shall form the joint committee of the european supervisory authorities (esas). within the european system of financial supervision, macroprudential supervision is carried out by the european systemic risk board (esrb). the main purpose of the european banking authority (eba) is to exchange information, coordinate the activities of national supervisory authorities and harmonise supervisory practices.
in writing. - according to the united nations, money laundering from illegal sources may account for nearly three percent of global gdp. this phenomenon is increasing year by year, and it is not limited to one country. criminals make various attempts to conceal their funds and then use them to finance further crimes, including terrorist attacks. i am glad that the european union is putting strong emphasis on stopping this kind of activity. this regulation contains provisions on the specific information required for transfers of funds exceeding eur 1 000. this should translate into a reduction in illicit money flows, benefiting the economy, the financial sector and, above all, society.

in writing. - the regulation lays down rules for payment service providers on the transmission of information on the payer and the payee throughout the payment chain in order to prevent crime, detect money laundering and terrorist financing and to better coordinate the activities of law enforcement authorities in the member states. the introduction of standardised procedures for financial institutions and payment service providers is essential to prevent money laundering, which costs the budget many billions of euros a year. in its report, the united nations office on drugs and crime (unodc) estimated that the flow of money laundering in the world today amounts to about 2.7% of global gdp.

in writing. - the legislative package on anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism is a response to the challenges faced by member states in this area. the organised nature of this criminal activity requires decisive and systematic action. this directive lays down rules applicable to companies, trusts, mutual insurance companies or foundations which may be used for money laundering. such institutions are often used to give credibility to the proceeds of crime. the planned transparency measures, such as the direct exposure list and the national central public registers of beneficial owners, should lead to a reduction in money laundering.
in writing. - in view of technological developments and globalisation, efforts to combat money laundering and terrorist financing should be systematic. our actions should seal and unify the financial systems in the member states in order to protect the national system from destabilisation. the phenomenon of money laundering and terrorist financing has an international dimension and therefore the solutions and measures adopted at community level should be subject to systematic review and to processes of harmonisation with those adopted by international bodies in order to ensure their high effectiveness.
in writing. - given that new legal regulations in the field of anti-money laundering and countering terrorist financing are already in force, it is worthwhile to reflect on the basic assumptions of these regulations and their practical effects on the institutions subject to them. this is all the more important as the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing has been seen in recent years as an effective way of combating crime. however, this is only one side of the coin; on the other hand, it is also an action that seriously interferes with civil rights and freedoms and generates costs and numerous burdensome obligations for entities covered by the scope of this regulation. without questioning the appropriateness of introducing certain solutions in poland since a certain legal situation is already a factual situation i would like to suggest practical ways of dealing with the new legal reality that has arisen as a result of the implementation of directive 2005/60/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 26 october 2005 on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering and terrorist financing into the polish legal system.

in writing. - the well-known benefits of e-invoicing have led several eu member states to require e-invoicing for public procurement. however, these bottom-up initiatives are dependent on national standards, most of which are not interoperable, which in turn can lead to an unnecessary complication of the procedure and an unnecessary increase in costs for companies wishing to participate in cross-border procurement. e-invoicing in europe is still very limited, accounting for only 4% to 15% of all invoices. in accordance with the commission legislative proposal presented in june 2013, a new european standard for e-invoicing will be developed by the european committee for standardisation (cen). the e-invoice is a necessary step towards the introduction of electronic public procurement procedures in the eu. concrete changes in this area will allow for more efficient use of public funds. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. - e-invoicing is an important step towards electronic document circulation in public administration (e-government) in europe one of the priorities of the digital agenda and can bring significant benefits to both the economy and the environment. the commission estimates that the adoption of e-invoicing in public procurement across the eu could bring savings of €2.3 billion. michel barnier, commissioner for internal market and services, said: ensuring that public administrations in the eu are modern and efficient is one of the european commission's priorities. the transition to e-procurement, and in particular to e-invoicing, can bring significant savings and facilitate the functioning of both governments and thousands of businesses operating in the internal market. the switch from paper documents to fully automated invoicing can reduce the cost of invoicing from eur 30-50 to eur 1. it's a good way to get the savings you need in this economy. as the public sector is the largest payer in the eu, it should play a leading role in promoting e-invoicing.

in writing. - organic farming is a management method that reduces dependence on external inputs by stimulating biological production mechanisms within the farm. organic farming radically reduces the use of industrially produced or processed products, even if they are analogues of substances found in nature. the aim of this system is to mimic processes in natural ecosystems both in terms of quality (type of substances put into circulation) and quantity (intensity level). there is no universally accepted definition of organic farming, and the system has been defined since its inception (around 1970) by criteria, i.e. the means and methods of production allowed.

in writing. - gender equality is not only a matter of diversity and social justice, but also a prerequisite for achieving the goals of sustainable economic growth, employment, competitiveness and social cohesion. investing in gender equality policies results in higher female employment rates, higher female share of gdp, tax revenues and sustainable fertility rates. it is important that gender equality remains at the core of the eu 2020 strategy, as equality between women and men has proven to be a lasting solution to old and new challenges. gender equality policy should therefore be seen as a long-term investment, not a short-term cost.
