madam president! i would like to say at the outset that i believe that a system of fiscal discipline is absolutely necessary in a monetary union in which the member states retain their fiscal powers and at the same time there is no system of fiscal transfers. so we need to develop a system of discipline based on clear rules. i want to remind you that the crisis in europe did not happen because the euro was introduced, but because some countries or some banking systems in some countries simply became over-indebted. but there was no obligation to go into debt. at the same time, i want to say that three years of experience with the six-pack and the two-pack shows that some adjustment is necessary in these instruments. first of all, i would like to point out that this is a system that is too complicated and complex not for experts, but for the general public. this type of system leaves room for a variety of interpretations, and i'll give you an example of the endless debate about the degree of flexibility in fiscal rules. the system should therefore be simplified to make it more understandable also for ordinary people. secondly, the system is too much based on political decisions. this concerns not only the political mechanism for the introduction of the excessive deficit procedure, but also the discussion on whether to extend the deadlines for the submission of the relevant documents for some countries, i.e. the largest countries. i think that if we have legal rules, then they should not be the subject of a political vote. thirdly, i also want to emphasize that the most important thing is national ownership. we cannot allow a situation in which politicians are constantly pointing to brussels and saying: brussels is telling us to impose some kind of fiscal discipline. no, fiscal discipline must be enshrined in national law in a way that is consistent across the european union and then politicians will be obliged to enforce national laws and regulations.
mr president, i would like to highlight three issues for vice-president dombrovskis. my first comment is that i believe the very nature of economic governance forces us to look beyond this six-pack and two-pack into areas such as, for example, the banking union; even if it is not an element of economic governance we all know that it can bring stability to the system and also influence the capacity of the emu to deliver. so when identifying the areas for improvement within economic governance, i think we have to have this broader perspective. my second comment is on rules versus procedures, and my colleague mr niedermayer alluded to this issue. i think that the economic governance framework has indeed put many rules in place but their success hinges on the right policy choices. we also know that citizens, when looking at the outcome of economic governance, do not differentiate between the policy choices – mostly made nationally – and the rules on which the system is based. this can of course raise doubts about the viability of the system as well as its democratic credentials. so i think that while respecting the rules, we also have to have better tailor-made policy choices and also we have to carefully assess and hopefully fill in the legitimacy gap. the third point is on growth. i think, in particular today, that any economic governance needs to have a strong growth perspective, and structural reforms are of the essence here; and yet the governance framework does not provide for a mechanism to foster those reforms. contractual arrangements which were proposed by the four presidents two years ago had until recently disappeared from the radar. the eurogroup conclusions from december seemed to reopen this issue, so i hope that we will also have a strong commitment as a catalyst for structural reforms. i also hope that the commission will push in this direction and will play a leading role in this issue.

the rapporteur. the commission has already decided to grant a discharge to the member states in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2000. this week we are finalising a very difficult process of budgetary agreement for 2014/2015, which includes an amendment to the european union's own resources regulation, which has been considered by the european parliament. i don't envy the participants of a conciliation i haven't attended for the first time in ten years. but i'm not jealous because there's always some additional circumstance of these negotiations, a part of the annual budget. last year, it was the link between the annual budget and the financial perspective agreements for 2014-2020. this year, the additional circumstance was the change in the way contributions were calculated based on gross national income and vat, which also complicated the negotiations. but year after year, the same problem arises: the draft budget of the european commission is not the commission's invention, it does not come out of nowhere. it's a downward-checked, conservative estimate of the estimate submissions coming in from 28 countries. hence the frustration in the final negotiations when this conservatively verified sum is then contested by the member states in the final negotiations. this year, the additional circumstance was indeed a significant change in the basis for calculating gross national product and vat, which meant good news for some countries overpaid, bad news for others underpaid. in the case of the united kingdom and the netherlands, these were considerable sums of money. the member states were so absorbed by this problem that they were unable to formulate their position by the end of the formal negotiating period, but at the same time they expected parliament to adopt an urgent procedure, a procedure for expressing a view in haste. we noted this paradox - budgetary delay on the one hand, urgency on the other - by accepting the opinions and the amendment to the own resources regulation as part of the final budgetary agreement. today we have an agreement for 2014/2015 and we also give a positive opinion on the amendment to the own resources regulation. however, we are introducing two amendments to the regulation in the interests of transparency in the financial and budgetary situation of the european union, namely the obligation to notify the european parliament of late payments and the result for the european budget. we are not renouncing criticism of the budgetary procedure itself, and that is the content of the legislative resolution. we would point out that these statistical changes were introduced by the member states themselves, in some cases facilitating their different settlements with the european commission. the iron rule, as i pointed out, has been to make the additional payments by december 1st. on the other hand, those countries which are extremely inflexible and do not make any concessions in the budgetary procedure, and are actually the leaders in cutting budgetary items that are clearly linked to economic competitiveness, job creation and growth, have called for facilitation and flexibility. this does not simplify the european union's own resources system. this complicates the system further, which is why the final element of our parliamentary position is to recognise the high-level group on own resources to actually review the system. the committee on budgets voted on the opinion last week. we expect to complete the formalities in the vote tomorrow.

madam president! autonomous trade preferences are an instrument provided for in the neighbourhood policy. we launch them when we find that we cannot help our partners in any other way, as in the case of moldova, except by introducing new trade tariffs that will allow us to obtain the export effects of the surpluses that have been located on the russian market. russia has obviously reacted this way because it is not satisfied with moldova's european aspirations. the association agreement between moldova and the european union, which creates a deep and comprehensive free trade area and a basis for economic liberalisation and broad economic reforms, also covers agricultural products. but these additional preferences allow for some liquidity in trade in moldova. this is particularly true for a significant proportion of those working in agriculture. we are pleased with what happened on 30 september in the elections in moldova. i had the opportunity to be in this country right before the election. our interlocutors have spoken with great concern about the consequences of the russian embargo and i think that a gesture from the european union, from the european parliament - this swift decision - could be very helpful to our partners in moldova.
in writing. following the signing of the eu/moldova association agreement on 27 june, russia banned the import of fruit from moldova, officially for phytosanitary reasons. the agricultural sector accounts for about 40 percent of moldova's economy, while horticulture is an important part of it, employing some 250,000 people, mostly in rural areas. under the dcfta, the union has committed itself to full liberalisation of market access for fresh fruit and vegetables, subject to certain quantities. in view of the current serious difficulties in moldova, the commission has proposed to temporarily increase this fully liberalised market access for imports of products from moldova into the eu. especially in the current geopolitical situation, it's hard to disagree with that conclusion. we must maintain good neighbourly relations, especially in this troubled part of europe.

mr. chairman, please! although slavery was only abolished in 1981, mauritania still lacks laws enforcing the ban. it is also worth noting that in mauritania it is hereditary and is associated with birth in this rather than another ethnic group. the european union cannot accept the violation of human rights, especially when it is happening in a country of the acp group with which it is cooperating. however, the efforts of outside countries are often not enough to change the status quo. first and foremost, the work of local activists is essential, hence my support for the work of biram dah abeid and other anti-slavery activists who have been imprisoned many times. i call for the release of biram dah abeid and the other abolitionists and for the nawakshut government to take a real stand against the slavery problem, because only by working towards democracy and stability will the european union be able to foster a fruitful relationship with mauritania and to support the development of that country.
mr. chairman, please! biram dah abeid is the leader of the anti-slavery initiative, which has about 9,000 activists. in 2013, he was awarded the united nations human rights prize for his work. sadly, on november 11, biram dah abeid along with 16 activists from his movement, after a peaceful march for the abolition of slavery, was convicted and imprisoned. we call for their immediate release. mauritania is a partner country of the european union under the acp association agreement. we therefore recall that the european union is opposed to slavery, child labour, mutilation and any other form of restriction of civil liberties. we call on the mauritanian government to respect its international commitments and to implement the relevant provisions to protect its own citizens. the european commission and the european external action service should strengthen their relations with the mauritanian authorities, which would allow the continuation of the mission of mauritanian activists to protect human rights and effectively combat the various forms of slavery.
mr. chairman, please! we are once again raising the issue of the persecution of human rights defenders by the security services in sudan in the european parliament. on december 6, 76-year-old dr. amin mekki medani, a well-known activist and advocate of the rule of law, was arrested. the arrest was in response to a declaration he signed on the 'establishment of a civil state and democracy', in which signatories, mainly from opposition parties, including the sudanese revolutionary front, call for an end to armed conflict in various regions of sudan, calling for legal, institutional and economic reforms. we strongly condemn the illegal detention of a seriously ill man, dr. medani, who is denied access to his medication. we call for his immediate release, as well as all other political prisoners. in light of the widespread repression in the country, we expect the sudanese authorities to end the unlawful detentions and to fulfil their obligations under the united nations declaration on the protection of fundamental civil liberties, including freedom of expression, assembly and religion.
in writing. once again, the european parliament draws public attention to sudan in its resolution. this african country, mired in the chaos of ongoing warfare and on the brink of humanitarian disaster, is moving further and further away from any international standards of respect for human rights. the unjustified arrest of dr. medani, a widely respected human rights activist, is a clear indication of this. looking at the situation in sudan, one can get the impression that the authorities of that country are working towards the destruction of the state and society. the restrictions on ngos trying to provide humanitarian aid to sudanese citizens in dire need are a sign that the sudanese authorities do not care about the lives of their own citizens. this country in the heart of africa is becoming a black spot on the world map, and unless the international community makes effective, peaceful efforts to resolve the conflicts in the region, the situation in sudan may soon prove to be destabilizing for the entire region. in calling for the unconditional release of dr medani, we also call on the sudanese authorities to come to their senses and change their attitude towards organizations and individuals who want to help the most needy in the country.
madam president! we have decided on the association between the european union and georgia and, of course, i voted in favour of the resolution, because anything that strengthens the independence of the countries of the east that emerged after the collapse of the soviet union fulfils the mandates of european solidarity. but i must express my disapproval of the fact that this solidarity is being denied by the imposition of a homosexual ideology on georgia. the social capital of europe was the georgian family march, which was attended by thousands of tbilisi residents at the invitation of the orthodox church. and the accusation of so-called homophobia against georgia is a real attack on the values enshrined in the law of central european countries, from lithuania to croatia. i would like to appeal in particular to the christian democrats: do not adopt the culture of the far left, vote as schuman, adenauer and de gasperi would have voted. and of course, joyeux noël, merry christmas and merry christmas to all of you.
